structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructure
structs.doc: Handle to an acceleration structure. See the "Ray tracing" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureAabbsDesc
structs.doc: Procedural (AABB) geometry within an acceleration structure build.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureBuildDesc
structs.doc: Describes one acceleration structure build (or update, if `src` is nonzero). `geometries` must match what was passed to `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes` when `dst` was sized.

fields.name: src
fields.doc: Zero handle for an initial build; the structure being updated for an in-place update.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureBuildRangeInfo
structs.doc: How many primitives (and at what offsets) each geometry in a build contributes. Index-aligned with the build's `geometries` array.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureBuildSizes
structs.doc: Buffer sizes needed to build an acceleration structure, returned by `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes`.

fields.name: acceleration_structure_size
fields.doc: Pass to `SturdyAccelerationStructureDesc::size`.

fields.name: build_scratch_size
fields.doc: Scratch buffer size needed for an initial build.

fields.name: update_scratch_size
fields.doc: Scratch buffer size needed for an in-place update (only meaningful with `STURDY_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_BUILD_FLAGS_ALLOW_UPDATE`).

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureDesc
structs.doc: Describes an acceleration structure to create. `size` must come from `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureGeometryDesc
structs.doc: One geometry entry in an acceleration structure build. `type` selects which of `triangles`/`aabbs`/`instances` is meaningful; the other two are ignored. Mirrors `RHI::AccelerationStructureGeometryDesc`, which carries all three as plain members rather than a tagged union.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance
structs.doc: One row of a top-level acceleration structure's instance buffer. Fixed 64-byte layout matching `VkAccelerationStructureInstanceKHR`/`D3D12_RAYTRACING_INSTANCE_DESC` exactly (and `RHI::AccelerationStructureInstance`) — write an array of these directly into a mapped/staged buffer bound as `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstancesDesc::buffer`.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc: Row-major 3x4 object-to-world transform (3 rows of 4 floats each).

fields.name: custom_index_and_mask
fields.doc: Packed via `sturdy_rhi_pack_instance_custom_index_and_mask`.

fields.name: shader_binding_table_offset_and_flags
fields.doc: Packed via `sturdy_rhi_pack_instance_sbt_offset_and_flags`.

fields.name: acceleration_structure_device_address
fields.doc: From `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_device_address` on the referenced bottom-level structure.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureInstancesDesc
structs.doc: Top-level instance geometry within an acceleration structure build.

fields.name: buffer
fields.doc: A buffer of `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance` records, or of pointers to them if `array_of_pointers` is set.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureTrianglesDesc
structs.doc: Triangle geometry within an acceleration structure build. `opacity_micromap` is a zero handle unless `Feature`-gated opacity micromaps are used (Vulkan only).

fields.name: transform_buffer
fields.doc: Zero handle means no per-instance transform.

structs.name: SturdyAdapterInfo
structs.doc:
Numeric identity of the adapter the engine selected.

Text fields (name, vendor, driver version, API version, stable device id) are read separately through `sturdy_rhi_adapter_string`, following the string-output convention above.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyAdapterInfo)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAmbientOcclusionSettings)` by `sturdy_ambient_occlusion_settings_init`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: World-space radius the occlusion search covers around a shaded point.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: Blend toward fully unoccluded. 1 = full strength, 0 = no occlusion.

fields.name: falloff_range
fields.doc: Fraction of `radius` over which an occluder fades out.

fields.name: thin_occluder_compensation
fields.doc: Thin-occluder compensation, in [0, 0.7].

fields.name: final_value_power
fields.doc: Contrast curve applied to the visibility term.

fields.name: sample_distribution_power
fields.doc: Exponent of the normalized sample-distance distribution.

fields.name: denoise
fields.doc: Runs the 5x5 edge-aware spatial denoiser.

structs.name: SturdyAnimationSet
structs.doc: Animation loaded from a file on its own (BVH mocap, or glTF/FBX with no mesh such as Mixamo downloads). Owned: valid until `sturdy_animation_set_release`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAntiAliasingSettings)` by `sturdy_anti_aliasing_settings_init`.

structs.name: SturdyAsset
structs.doc:
An engine asset — a shader, model or texture.

Opaque by value: the bytes are the engine's own asset handle, copied in and out rather than interpreted. Copy it freely, compare it with `memcmp`, and treat a zeroed value as invalid. It stays valid for as long as the engine that produced it.

structs.name: SturdyAsyncObject
structs.doc: A long-lived object (connection, listener, server, file, ...). Owned until `sturdy_object_release`, which closes it.

structs.name: SturdyAsyncOp
structs.doc: A pending or finished operation. Owned until `sturdy_op_release`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAudioConfig)`.

fields.name: sample_rate
fields.doc: 0 selects 48000.

fields.name: channel_count
fields.doc: Used with `STURDY_AUDIO_LAYOUT_CHANNEL_COUNT`.

fields.name: max_voices
fields.doc: 0 selects the defaults (8192 voices, 4096 audible at once, helper threads chosen by the engine).

fields.name: open_device
fields.doc: Open the default playback device. False mixes silently (headless tools, tests, or when a custom sink takes the output).

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAutoExposureSettings)` by `sturdy_auto_exposure_settings_init`.

fields.name: min_log2_luminance
fields.doc: Luminance range the histogram meters, as log2(scene-linear luminance).

fields.name: low_percent
fields.doc: Fractions of the metered pixel mass ignored at the dark / bright end (`0 < = low < high < = 1`).

fields.name: key_value
fields.doc: Luminance the metered average is mapped to (middle grey).

fields.name: compensation_ev
fields.doc: Exposure compensation in stops.

fields.name: adapt_up_speed
fields.doc: Adaptation rates per second when the scene darkens (exposure rises) / brightens.

fields.name: center_weight
fields.doc: 0 = every pixel counts equally, 1 = the frame edges count for nothing.

fields.name: structure_stride
fields.doc: Structured-buffer element stride. Only meaningful for a storage-buffer binding on backends that need it (D3D12 structured buffers); leave 0 otherwise.

structs.name: SturdyBindGroupLayout

structs.name: SturdyBindGroupLayoutDesc
structs.doc: Describes a bind group layout to create.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyBindGroupLayoutDesc)` by the caller.

fields.name: label

structs.name: SturdyBindGroupLayoutEntry
structs.doc: One binding slot within a bind group layout.

fields.doc: D3D-style shader register this binding compiles to. Ignored on Vulkan; leave at `0xffffffff` (the default) when only targeting Vulkan.

fields.name: visibility
fields.doc: Bitwise OR of `STURDY_SHADER_STAGE_*`.

fields.name: struct_size

structs.name: SturdyBuffer
structs.doc: Handle to a GPU buffer. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyBufferBarrier
structs.doc: A pipeline barrier scoped to one buffer range.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Zero means the buffer's remaining size from `offset`.

structs.name: SturdyBufferCopy

structs.name: SturdyBufferTextureCopy
structs.doc: Describes one buffer < ->texture copy region.

fields.name: buffer_image_height

structs.name: SturdyBytesSink
structs.doc: Where a stream callback writes the item it produces (copied immediately).

fields.name: internal

structs.name: SturdyBytesView

fields.name: struct_size

fields.name: fisheye_strength
fields.doc: Barrel distortion, 0 = none; the image is zoomed so the corners still reach the frame edge.

fields.name: chromatic_aberration

fields.name: sensor_noise

fields.name: lut_texture

fields.name: struct_size

fields.name: struct_size

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: A `SturdyFieldKind`.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: Number of consecutive values; must be nonzero.

structs.name: SturdyComponentFieldInfo
structs.doc: One field of a registered component, as read back.

fields.name: struct_size

structs.doc: One component's initial value, for `sturdy_ecs_spawn`.

structs.name: SturdyEngine
structs.doc:
Borrowed reference to the live engine, valid only inside the callback that received it.

A struct wrapping an integer rather than a raw pointer: the integer is a token that is minted when a callback begins and revoked when it returns, and tokens are never reused. A stale token therefore always resolves to "expired" instead of aliasing a later object.

structs.name: SturdyEntity
structs.doc:
Identifies an entity.

The `generation` half is what makes a stale handle safe: entity indices are recycled after a destroy, so an entity value kept from an earlier frame can name a live row belonging to someone else. Every call below checks the generation and reports `STURDY_ERROR_ENTITY_NOT_ALIVE` rather than acting on the wrong entity. A zeroed `SturdyEntity` is never alive.

structs.name: SturdyFeatureSupport
structs.doc: Whether a feature is available, with the reason when it is not (or only partly). `note` is a static string owned by the engine: it stays valid for the life of the process; it is empty when the feature is fully supported.

fields.name: pattern

Same scope and reuse rules as `SturdyEngine`. Valid only inside `request_render_frame`.

structs.name: SturdyFrameExtents

structs.name: SturdyGameLogic
structs.doc:
Callbacks implementing your application, mirroring the C++ `Engine::GameLogic` interface.

Every callback may be null; a null callback behaves as a no-op that neither fails nor renders. `user_data` is passed back to each callback untouched and is never interpreted by the engine.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyGameLogic)`.

fields.name: user_data
fields.doc: Opaque pointer handed back to every callback below.

fields.name: on_engine_initialized
fields.doc: Called once after the engine and its first window are live, before any frame.

fields.name: request_render_frame
fields.doc:
Called once per frame per surface to describe what should be drawn.

Configure `frame` with the `sturdy_frame_*` setters, then return `STURDY_TRUE` to render it. Return `STURDY_FALSE` to skip this frame entirely — the correct answer when there is nothing new to show, since it presents no frame rather than presenting a blank one.

`frame` arrives pre-populated with the engine's standard render pipeline and a camera whose aspect ratio already matches this surface, so a caller that configures nothing still produces a complete frame. Every setter overrides part of that starting point.

fields.name: on_shutdown
fields.doc: Called once during teardown, before the engine is destroyed. Failures cannot be reported from here; shutdown proceeds regardless.

fields.name: destroy
fields.doc: Called exactly once after `on_shutdown`, to release whatever `user_data` owns. This is the hook a binding uses to drop its language-side object (a boxed Rust struct, a pinned GC handle) at a well-defined point rather than leaking it.

structs.name: SturdyGameModule

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyGameModule)`.

fields.name: after_count
fields.doc: Number of entries in `after`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Unique, non-empty, null-terminated UTF-8 name that other modules' `after` lists refer to. Copied.

fields.name: after
fields.doc: Names of modules that must start before this one and shut down after it. May be null when `after_count` is 0. Unknown names and cycles are reported when the modules start (see `sturdy_runtime_run_modules`).

fields.name: contributes_scene
fields.doc: Nonzero: this module may supply the scene (camera, lighting, render graph) for a frame. Zero: overlay-only, so its overlay passes are drawn but it never replaces the scene.

fields.name: logic
fields.doc: The module's callbacks, with `struct_size` set as for `sturdy_runtime_run`.

structs.name: SturdyGltfInstance
structs.doc:
One placement of a model within an imported scene.

A glTF file can reference the same mesh from many nodes, so several instances may carry the same `model` with different transforms. Spawning one entity per instance is what reproduces the scene as authored.

structs.name: SturdyGltfScene
structs.doc:
An imported glTF scene: its models, the node instances that place them, and its lights.

Unlike `SturdyEngine` and `SturdyFrame`, this handle is **owned, not borrowed**. It stays valid until you pass it to `sturdy_gltf_release`, which is the one thing on this ABI you must explicitly free. Releasing it does not destroy the models it produced — those belong to the engine's asset manager and outlive the scene, which is what lets you keep spawning them.

structs.name: SturdyGpuInfo
structs.doc:
One physical GPU this machine can create an engine on, as reported by `sturdy_gpu_enumerate`.

Unlike other queries in this header, `name`/`vendor`/`physical_device_id` are fixed-size buffers embedded directly in this struct rather than following the general string-output convention above (buffer + capacity + `*out_length`, queried by calling twice): enumeration itself creates and tears down a temporary graphics instance per backend, so asking a second time to learn a string's length would pay that cost again and risks a different snapshot (a GPU unplugged between calls) coming back. Values are always null-terminated, truncated rather than overflowed if a driver-reported string is unusually long.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyGpuInfo)` by the engine.

fields.name: physical_device_id
fields.doc: Pass as `SturdyRuntimeConfig::physical_device_id` to request this GPU.

fields.doc: ...and send this many (needs `limit_body_length`); otherwise to the end of the file.

fields.name: max_connections_per_ip

fields.name: shutdown_timeout_ms

fields.doc: The state the previous generation of this plugin stored with `set_state`, or null. Ownership moves to this generation: the previous generation's `UNLOAD` sees null. fields.name: is_container
fields.doc: True when the field is a recognized container (`std::vector <T >` with a trivially-copyable `T`, in the current engine) — see the container section below.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionId
structs.doc: Identifies a reflected type, field, method, event, or enum. Derived from its canonical name and stable for the process lifetime (or until unregistered) — the same shape as `SturdyResourceId`, since both wrap the engine's underlying 128-bit name hash identically.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionMethodInfo
structs.doc: What the engine knows about a reflected method.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyReflectionMethodInfo)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: is_static
fields.doc: True for a static member function — call it with `sturdy_reflection_invoke_static_method` instead of the instance version.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionSettings
structs.doc: Indirect specular light (since 0.33): the sky prefiltered per roughness (so every surface reflects something and metals are never black) plus deterministic (noise-free) screen-space reflections with cone-traced glossiness, which replace it where the reflected surface is on screen. On by default.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyReflectionSettings)` by `sturdy_reflection_settings_init`.

fields.name: max_roughness
fields.doc: Surfaces rougher than this (perceptual roughness) use only the environment.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc: How far behind the depth buffer a surface is assumed to extend, as a fraction of its view depth.

fields.name: glossy_blur
fields.doc: Scales how fast the specular cone widens with distance (1 = the GGX lobe).

structs.name: SturdyReflectionSubscription
structs.doc: Handle to an installed before-hook/after-hook/event-listener subscription, for later removal with the matching `_remove_*`/`_unsubscribe_event` call. Not scope-bound — stays valid until explicitly removed or the type it was installed on is unregistered.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionTypeBuilder
structs.doc: Handle to an in-progress type description. Owned by the caller — build it up with the `_add_*` calls below, then either `_finish` it (consuming the builder, registering the type) or `_discard` it (consuming the builder without registering anything).

fields.name: use_tls
fields.doc: Wrap the hop to the relay in TLS (hides tokens and metadata from the network).

fields.name: max_sessions
fields.doc: 0: 1024 joined sessions / 1024 waiting connections / 16 waiting per address.

fields.name: pair_timeout_ms
fields.doc: 0: 30 s a peer waits for its partner; 0: 120 s idle limit on a joined session.

fields.name: max_session_bytes
fields.doc: Cut a session after this many relayed bytes; 0: unlimited.

fields.name: max_token_bytes
fields.doc: Longest rendezvous token accepted; 0: 128.

structs.name: SturdyRenderBundle
structs.doc: Handle to a finished, replayable render bundle. Unlike the encoder that produced it, this carries no scope of its own — like `SturdyBuffer`, it is an informational identifier the RHI device owns and validates until `sturdy_rhi_destroy_render_bundle`.

structs.name: SturdyRenderBundleDesc
structs.doc: Describes a render bundle to create. Bundles are format-only — they record against whatever render pass later executes them, matching it by attachment formats/sample count/view mask rather than by binding real attachments.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderBundleDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_desc_init`.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: Sample count as an integer (1, 2, 4, 8, or 16), matching `RHI::SampleCount`'s values.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyRenderBundleEncoder
structs.doc: Owned handle to an in-progress bundle recording, borrowed from the engine's active device. Lives until `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_finish` or `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_release`.

structs.name: SturdyRenderPassDesc
structs.doc: Describes a render pass to begin.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderPassDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_desc_init`.

fields.name: allow_bundles
fields.doc: Must be true to call `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_execute_bundles` on the pass this creates.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyRenderPassEncoder
structs.doc: Owned handle to an in-progress render pass, borrowed from its command encoder. Lives until `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end`. The parent `SturdyCommandEncoder` may not be used for anything else while a pass is open.

structs.name: SturdyRenderPipeline
structs.doc: Handle to a render pipeline. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyRenderPipelineDesc
structs.doc:
Everything needed to build a raster pipeline against dynamic rendering (no render-pass object). Viewport/scissor are always dynamic, set per-draw on the render pass encoder, so they are not part of this description. All array fields are read synchronously during `sturdy_rhi_create_render_pipeline` and need not outlive the call.

Set `mesh` (and optionally `task`) for a mesh-shader pipeline, or set `vertex` for a traditional vertex-input pipeline — not both. A mesh pipeline requires the `"mesh shaders"` feature (check with `sturdy_rhi_feature_index`/`sturdy_rhi_feature_enabled`) and ignores `vertex_buffers`/`topology`; a task stage additionally requires `"task/amplification shaders"`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderPipelineDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_render_pipeline_desc_init`.

fields.name: fragment
fields.doc: Module may be the zero handle for a depth-only pipeline.

fields.name: depth_stencil
fields.doc: `format` field `STURDY_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` means no depth/stencil attachment.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

fields.name: task
fields.doc: Amplification/task stage for a mesh-shader pipeline. Zero handle means no task stage.

fields.name: mesh
fields.doc: Mesh stage. A valid (nonzero) module here selects the mesh-shader pipeline path instead of `vertex`.

structs.name: SturdyRenderTextureDesc
structs.doc:
Describes a texture built directly from raw pixels, for `sturdy_render_create_texture`.

Named distinctly from the RHI-level `SturdyTextureDesc` (see "RHI resources" below) even though both describe "a texture to create": that one configures a raw GPU resource (`SturdyFormat`, mip levels, usage flags, no pixel data), while this one is the asset-manager-level counterpart to `sturdy_render_load_texture` — pixels in, a `SturdyAsset` usable with `sturdy_render_set_model_texture` out.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderTextureDesc)` by `sturdy_render_texture_desc_init`.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Capped well below any real GPU's maximum, only to keep `width * height * 4` from overflowing while validating this struct — the real limit is `SturdyDeviceLimits::max_texture_dimension_2d`.

fields.name: rgba8
fields.doc: RGBA8 pixel data, `width * height * 4` bytes, row-major and tightly packed (no row padding). Copied before this call returns; the pointer need not outlive it.

structs.name: SturdyResourceId
structs.doc: Identifies a resource or event type. Derived from its canonical name and stable across runs.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRestirGiSettings)` by `sturdy_restir_gi_settings_init`.

fields.name: multi_bounce_feedback
fields.doc: Damping (0-1) applied to last frame's lit scene color when read back as an extra indirect term. 0 disables multi-bounce feedback.

fields.name: svgf_atrous_iterations
fields.doc: Only read when `denoiser` is `STURDY_RESTIR_GI_DENOISER_SVGF`.

structs.name: SturdyRuntimeConfig
structs.doc:
Application and window configuration for `sturdy_runtime_run`.

Populate with `sturdy_runtime_config_init` first — that sets `struct_size` and every default — then override only the fields you care about. String fields are borrowed UTF-8 and must stay alive for the duration of the `sturdy_runtime_run` call; the engine copies what it needs.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRuntimeConfig)`. `sturdy_runtime_config_init` does this for you.

fields.name: app_name
fields.doc: Application name reported to the graphics driver. Null selects the engine default.

fields.name: window_title
fields.doc: Initial title of the primary window. Null selects the engine default.

fields.name: shaders_directory
fields.doc: Directory the engine loads shaders from, relative to the working directory unless absolute. Null selects `"Shaders"`.

fields.name: window_width
fields.doc: Primary window client-area size in physical pixels.

fields.name: enable_raytracing
fields.doc: Request ray-tracing support at device creation. Initialization fails if the selected adapter cannot provide it, rather than silently continuing without — features that depend on it (ReSTIR GI) would otherwise fail confusingly at first use.

fields.name: enable_shader_disk_cache
fields.doc: Cache compiled shaders on disk between runs.

fields.name: enable_native_access
fields.doc: Publish the backend's raw Vulkan or D3D12 objects, making the `sturdy_native_*` family usable. Off by default and opt-in on purpose: it is the one part of this ABI that hands out pointers the engine's own invariants do not cover, so a build that never asks for it cannot accidentally come to depend on native access.

fields.name: physical_device_id
fields.doc:
Selects a specific GPU by the stable identifier reported through `STURDY_ADAPTER_STRING_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_ID`. Null or empty lets the engine pick.

This is the other half of persisting a user's GPU choice: read the id from a previous run's adapter, store it, and pass it back here. Identifiers agree across Vulkan and D3D12 for the same physical device, so a choice made under one backend still resolves under the other.

An id that matches no device on this machine **fails startup** with `STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` rather than quietly selecting a different GPU — the engine treats an explicit device request as a requirement, not a hint. Hardware does change between runs, so an application persisting this value should be prepared to clear it and retry with null once, instead of treating the failure as fatal.

structs.name: SturdySampler
structs.doc: Handle to a sampler. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdySamplerDesc
structs.doc: Describes a sampler to create.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdySamplerDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_sampler_desc_init`.

fields.name: max_anisotropy
fields.doc: Zero disables anisotropic filtering.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdySceneSettings)` by `sturdy_scene_settings_init`.

fields.name: background_intensity
fields.doc: Multiplier applied to the background color/environment when nothing else occludes a ray.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyScreenSpaceGiSettings)` by `sturdy_screen_space_gi_settings_init`.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Screen-space indirect lighting (no ray tracing needed, every backend). Used when ReSTIR GI is off.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far, in world units, a surface can light its neighbours.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc: Assumed thickness of what the depth buffer shows, in world units.

fields.name: slice_count
fields.doc: Search directions per pixel and depth taps per direction (at half resolution).

fields.name: temporal_alpha
fields.doc: Weight of the newest frame in the temporal accumulation.

fields.name: max_radiance
fields.doc: Brightest scene-linear luminance a texel may contribute.

structs.name: SturdyScriptInstance
structs.doc: A running script: callbacks plus the pointer they work on. Every callback may be null (a no-op). Fill it in `SturdyScriptLanguage::load`, or pass it to `sturdy_script_module_create_native`. Callbacks must not unwind.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyScriptInstance)`.

fields.name: user_data
fields.doc: Passed to every callback below.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Runs once when the script starts. Return `STURDY_FALSE` to abort the load; write the reason to `error` (see `sturdy_bytes_sink_set`).

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Runs once per engine update, at the update boundary, in module start order.

fields.name: request_render_frame
fields.doc: Contributes to a frame exactly like `SturdyGameLogic::request_render_frame`. May run on a render thread.

fields.name: stop
fields.doc: Runs once when the script is unloaded or replaced, after `save_state`.

fields.name: save_state
fields.doc: Hot reload: write the state to hand to the replacement into `out` and return `STURDY_TRUE`, or return `STURDY_FALSE` for none.

fields.name: restore_state
fields.doc: Receives the previous version's state before `start`. Return `STURDY_FALSE` to refuse it (the reload fails and the script stays unloaded).

fields.name: call
fields.doc: Calls a function the script exposes. Write the result to `result` (or the reason to `error`) and return whether it worked.

fields.name: on_message
fields.doc: A message sent to this script or published on a topic it subscribed to.

fields.name: destroy
fields.doc: Releases `user_data`, exactly once, after `stop` (or if the script never started).

structs.name: SturdyScriptLanguage
structs.doc: A language adapter an application registers to run scripts in an interpreter it provides.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyScriptLanguage)`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name `SturdyScriptSource::language` refers to. Copied.

fields.name: extensions
fields.doc: File extensions with the dot (".lua") that select this language. May be null.

fields.name: load
fields.doc: Parses or compiles `source` into `out_instance` (struct_size set by you). Return `STURDY_FALSE` with the reason in `error` when it does not load. The instance must not start running yet. Called with the script lock held.

fields.name: destroy
fields.doc: Releases `user_data` once the adapter is unregistered and every script it loaded is gone. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyScriptMessage
structs.doc: A message between scripts. Valid only during `on_message`.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: The sending script; empty when the host application sent it.

structs.name: SturdyScriptModuleDesc
structs.doc: A script as a module: where it comes from and where it sits in the start order.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyScriptModuleDesc)`.

fields.name: after
fields.doc: Modules that must start before this one (and shut down after it).

fields.name: contributes_scene
fields.doc: Nonzero: the script may supply the scene for a frame; zero (the usual): it never replaces the scene.

structs.name: SturdyScriptSource
structs.doc: Describes where a script comes from. Strings are copied unless noted.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyScriptSource)`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Unique, non-empty. The script is a module of this name.

fields.name: language
fields.doc: The language adapter ("lua", "js"). Null or empty: chosen from `path`'s extension.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: A file the adapter may read, and the extension that picks a language. May be null.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The source text or bytecode. Empty (null): the adapter loads `path`.

fields.name: options
fields.doc: Adapter-specific settings (a module root, strict mode, ...). May be null.

structs.name: SturdyScriptTick
structs.doc: One engine update as a script sees it.

structs.name: SturdySemaphore
structs.doc: Handle to a timeline semaphore: a GPU-to-GPU (and GPU-to-host, via `sturdy_rhi_wait_semaphore`) synchronization primitive that counts up through a sequence of `u64` values rather than toggling once like a fence. Reach for this to order work across two queues (e.g. an upload on the transfer queue that a graphics-queue submission must wait on); use `SturdyFence` instead for the common "wait for this one submission to finish on the host" case. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdySemaphoreDesc
structs.doc: Describes a semaphore to create.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdySemaphoreDesc)` by the caller.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdySemaphoreSignal
structs.doc: One semaphore a submission signals once its work completes.

fields.name: stages
fields.doc: Pipeline stages of this submission that must complete before signaling. Bitwise OR of `STURDY_PIPELINE_STAGE_*`.

structs.name: SturdySemaphoreWait
structs.doc: One semaphore a submission waits on before its work begins.

fields.name: stages
fields.doc: Pipeline stages of this submission that must wait; other stages may start immediately. Bitwise OR of `STURDY_PIPELINE_STAGE_*`.

structs.name: SturdyShaderBindingTableRegion
structs.doc: One shader binding table region: a byte range in a buffer holding shader group handles written by `sturdy_rhi_write_ray_tracing_shader_group_handles`. `stride` is ignored for `raygen` (a single record); `miss`/`hit`/`callable` are strided tables.

structs.name: SturdyShaderEntry
structs.doc: A shader module plus the stage and entry point a pipeline invokes it at.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.doc: Defaults to "main" if left null.

structs.name: SturdyShaderModule
structs.doc: Handle to a shader module compiled from raw backend bytecode (SPIR-V on Vulkan, DXIL on D3D12). This is the low-level counterpart to `sturdy_render_load_shader`, which additionally invokes the engine's Slang toolchain; use this one when bytecode was already compiled offline. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyShaderModuleDesc
structs.doc: Describes a shader module to create from raw bytecode.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyShaderModuleDesc)` by the caller.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyShadowSettings)` by `sturdy_shadow_settings_init`.

fields.name: atlas_size
fields.doc: Edge size of the shared spot/point shadow atlas.

fields.name: cascade_blend
fields.doc: Fraction of a cascade's view-space depth range spent cross-fading into the next cascade.

fields.name: cascade_resolutions
fields.doc: Per-cascade shadow-map edge resolution, near cascade first.

fields.name: filter_radius_texels
fields.doc: PCF filter radius in shadow texels of the sampled cascade.

fields.name: normal_bias
fields.doc: Receiver normal-offset magnitude in shadow texels at normal incidence.

fields.name: contact_shadow_intensity
fields.doc: Maximum darkening the contact term may apply, in [0, 1].

structs.name: SturdyShapeParams
structs.doc:
Dimensions for a built-in shape. Only the fields listed for the chosen shape are read.

Initialize with `sturdy_render_shape_params_init`, which fills the same defaults the engine's C++ primitives use, then override what you care about.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyShapeParams)`.

fields.name: capped
fields.doc: Whether cylinders and cones get end caps.

structs.name: SturdySpawnOptions
structs.doc: How `sturdy_scene_spawn` places and starts a scene.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdySpawnOptions)`.

fields.name: auto_play
fields.doc: Start playing as soon as the entities exist.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: Loop the starting clip.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: Playback speed multiplier.

fields.name: initial_clip
fields.doc: Clip to start with, or null for the file's first.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc: Column-major 4x4 transform applied on top of the file's own placement (identity to keep it as authored).

structs.name: SturdySseEvent
structs.doc: One Server-Sent Event. Line breaks in `event` and `id` are dropped, so a hostile value cannot inject fields.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: May contain newlines; each line becomes a `data:` field. Null-terminated.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: Optional event name and last-event-id.

fields.name: retry_ms
fields.doc: Reconnect delay hint, sent when `has_retry`.

structs.name: SturdyStaticFilesOptions
structs.doc: Static file serving options. Zero means the default noted.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: Directory served; files outside it are unreachable, including through symlinks. Required.

fields.name: index_file
fields.doc: Served for a request naming a directory; null: "index.html".

fields.name: cache_control
fields.doc: Sent as Cache-Control; null: "public, max-age=300".

fields.name: allow_dotfiles
fields.doc: Files and directories starting with '.' are hidden (404) unless set.

fields.name: follow_symlinks
fields.doc: Allow symlinks that point outside `root` (a link planted in the tree must not expose the disk).

fields.name: no_precompressed
fields.doc: Do not serve `name.br` / `name.gz` siblings to clients that accept them.

fields.name: spa_fallback
fields.doc: Served (status 200) when nothing matches a GET — single-page-app routing. null: 404.

fields.name: mime_types
fields.doc: Extra or overriding MIME mappings (name = extension with dot, value = type).

structs.name: SturdyStencilFaceState
structs.doc: Stencil behavior for one face (front or back).

structs.name: SturdySurface
structs.doc:
Identifies the render surface (window) a frame is being produced for.

Opaque and informational in this ABI version: use it to tell surfaces apart across callbacks when an application has multiple windows. It carries no lifetime of its own.

structs.name: SturdySystem
structs.doc: Handle to a system registered through `sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex`.

structs.name: SturdySystemAccess
structs.doc: One component a system operates on, and how.

structs.name: SturdySystemResourceAccess
structs.doc: One resource or event channel a system operates on, and how.

structs.name: SturdyTask
structs.doc:
A running background task.

Owned like `SturdyGltfScene`, not scope-bound: it stays valid until `sturdy_async_release`. Releasing does **not** cancel the task — there is no cancellation — it only says you are done observing it. A task whose handle has been released still runs to completion, so whatever its `user_data` points at must stay alive until the task itself finishes.

structs.name: SturdyTaskInput
structs.doc: What the previous stage of an execution chain produced.

structs.name: SturdyTaskOutput
structs.doc: Where a task's result is written from inside its callback (copied immediately).

fields.name: internal
fields.doc: Engine-private; do not touch.

structs.name: SturdyTextInputArea
structs.doc: Screen-space hint for where an IME should draw its candidate/composition window, in window coordinates (the same units as `SturdyWindowSnapshot::width`/`height` and mouse positions). `cursor_offset_x` is the caret's offset from `x` within that area, for IMEs that anchor the popup to caret position rather than the area's top-left corner.

structs.name: SturdyTextInputOptions
structs.doc: What kind of text a field takes, for IMEs and on-screen keyboards. Populate with `sturdy_text_input_options_init`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyTextInputOptions)` before the call.

structs.name: SturdyTexture
structs.doc: Handle to a GPU texture. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyTextureBarrier
structs.doc: A pipeline barrier scoped to one texture's subresources, optionally also transitioning its layout.

structs.name: SturdyTextureCopy
structs.doc: One texture-to-texture copy region. Source and destination subresources must have the same dimensions.

structs.name: SturdyTextureDesc
structs.doc: Describes a texture to create.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyTextureDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_texture_desc_init`.

fields.name: depth_or_layers
fields.doc: Depth for a 3D texture, array layer count for a 1D/2D texture.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: MSAA sample count. Must be 1 for anything but a 2D color/depth-stencil attachment.

fields.name: usage
fields.doc: Bitwise OR of `STURDY_TEXTURE_USAGE_*`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyTextureSubresourceRange
structs.doc: Identifies the mip/array subrange a clear or barrier applies to.

fields.name: mip_level_count
fields.doc: `STURDY_ALL_REMAINING` covers every remaining mip level.

fields.name: array_layer_count
fields.doc: `STURDY_ALL_REMAINING` covers every remaining array layer.

structs.name: SturdyTextureView
structs.doc: Handle to a texture view. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyTextureViewDesc
structs.doc: Describes a texture view to create.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyTextureViewDesc)` by the caller.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: `STURDY_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` reuses the texture's own format.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyTlsClientOptions
structs.doc: How to verify a server (client side of TLS/QUIC/HTTPS/WSS). Chain and host name are always checked unless `pinned_sha256` names the exact certificate(s) accepted.

fields.name: server_name
fields.doc: Name sent as SNI and checked against the certificate; null: the host being connected to.

fields.name: no_system_roots
fields.doc: Do not trust the operating system's roots (use `ca_pem` only).

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.doc: Extra trusted CA certificates, PEM (may hold several). May be null.

fields.name: pinned_sha256
fields.doc: Hex SHA-256 of acceptable leaf certificates; when present they replace chain validation.

fields.name: identify_peer_by_certificate_only
fields.doc: Peer-to-peer opt-in: accept any certificate and let **you** compare `peer_sha256`. Never default.

fields.name: client_certificate_pem
fields.doc: Client certificate for mutual TLS (both or neither).

fields.name: alpn
fields.doc: ALPN protocols to offer, most preferred first.

fields.name: handshake_timeout_ms
fields.doc: Time allowed for the TLS handshake; 0: 10 s.

structs.name: SturdyTlsServerOptions
structs.doc: How to present and check identities on the accepting side.

fields.name: client_ca_pem
fields.doc: CAs whose client certificates are accepted (mutual TLS). May be null.

fields.name: accept_any_client_certificate
fields.doc: Peer-to-peer opt-in: accept any self-signed client certificate; authorise by `peer_sha256` yourself.

fields.name: handshake_timeout_ms
fields.doc: Time allowed for each client's TLS handshake; 0: 10 s.

structs.name: SturdyToneMappingSettings
structs.doc: Fine-grained tone-mapping settings. `sturdy_frame_set_tone_mapping` remains the quick path for just operator/exposure/white-point/saturation; use this instead to also reach HDR display mapping and the AGX/Hermite-spline/PsychoV curve-tuning knobs, which only apply when `operation` selects the matching operator.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyToneMappingSettings)` by `sturdy_tone_mapping_settings_init`.

fields.name: hdr_paper_white_nits
fields.doc: SDR/HDR mapping reference white, in nits.

fields.name: hdr_peak_nits
fields.doc: HDR display peak brightness, in nits.

fields.name: agx_look
fields.doc: Only read when `operation` is `STURDY_TONE_MAPPING_AGX`.

structs.name: SturdyVulkanHandles
structs.doc:
The engine's raw Vulkan objects.

Fields are `void *` rather than `VkInstance` and friends so this header stays standalone — it must be includable by a caller that has no Vulkan SDK, and by one that has a different version than the engine was built against. Cast each field to its documented type.

**Every handle is borrowed.** The engine owns them and destroys them at shutdown. Do not destroy them, and do not use them after the engine is gone. Anything you do with them sits outside the engine's own synchronization: if you submit work on these queues or record into the device, you are responsible for not racing the engine's frame loop.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyVulkanHandles)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: instance
fields.doc: `VkInstance`.

fields.name: physical_device
fields.doc: `VkPhysicalDevice`.

fields.name: device
fields.doc: `VkDevice`.

fields.name: graphics_queue
fields.doc: `VkQueue` for the primary graphics lane.

fields.name: debounce_ms
fields.doc: Bursts of writes within this window become one event; 0: 50 ms.

fields.name: force_polling
fields.doc: Use the portable polling backend even where the OS offers events.

fields.name: poll_interval_ms
fields.doc: The polling backend's scan period; 0: 250 ms.

fields.name: max_pending_events
fields.doc: Events buffered before an overflow event is reported; 0: 4096.

structs.name: SturdyWebGpuHandles
structs.doc:
The engine's raw WebGPU objects.

Fields are `void *` for the same reason as `SturdyVulkanHandles`/`SturdyD3D12Handles`, and carry the same borrowing rules. Unlike those two, this deliberately stops at the WebGPU objects themselves rather than reaching beneath them to whatever native API Dawn chose (Vulkan, Metal, or D3D12) -- that is fundamentally unavailable on the Web target (a browser's WebGPU implementation exposes no native handles to any embedder) and would defeat the point of the backend even on native Dawn. Cast each field to its documented `webgpu.h` type. There is exactly one queue: WebGPU has no separate graphics/compute/transfer queues to distinguish, so there is no `sturdy_native_webgpu_queue` counterpart to `sturdy_native_vulkan_queue`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyWebGpuHandles)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: instance
fields.doc: `WGPUInstance`.

fields.name: adapter
fields.doc: `WGPUAdapter`.

fields.name: device
fields.doc: `WGPUDevice`.

fields.name: queue
fields.doc: `WGPUQueue`, the one queue every WebGPU device exposes.

fields.name: timeout_ms
fields.doc: 0: 30 s for resolve + connect + TLS + upgrade.

fields.name: max_message_bytes
fields.doc: 0: 1 MiB. Bigger incoming messages close the socket with 1009.

fields.name: max_queued_send_bytes
fields.doc: 0: 4 MiB of unsent data before `send` fails with `STURDY_IO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

fields.name: idle_timeout_ms
fields.doc: 0: 60 s without inbound traffic drops the connection (pings keep healthy idle links alive).

fields.name: compression
fields.doc: Negotiate permessage-deflate (the inflated size is bounded by `max_message_bytes`).

fields.name: inbox_messages
fields.doc: Received messages buffered before reading pauses; 0: 16.

fields.name: handshake_timeout_ms
fields.doc: Time allowed for the opening handshake; 0: 10 s.

fields.name: use_tls
fields.doc: Serve wss:// with `tls` instead of ws://.

structs.name: SturdyWindowSnapshot
structs.doc:
Observed state of one window this frame.

`width`/`height` are window coordinates (the space mouse positions and `position_x/y` use) and `framebuffer_width/height` are physical pixels. They are equal on Windows/X11 and differ on macOS, scaled Wayland and the Web. Render with the framebuffer values. The display's UI scale is separate; read it with `sturdy_window_content_scale`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyWindowSnapshot)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: surface_id

callbacks.name: SturdyArcDestroyFn
callbacks.doc: Frees a foreign pointer owned by an arc. Runs once, when the last reference goes away, on whichever thread dropped it.

callbacks.name: SturdyAsyncOpFn
callbacks.doc: Called when an operation finishes. Runs on a network, timer or worker thread. The op is still owned by you; read its result here or later. Called exactly once for every registration — also when the op was released or cancelled meanwhile, so the `user_data` you attached can always be freed here. In that case `op` is no longer a valid handle (its getters report an expired handle); check with `sturdy_op_status` first.

callbacks.name: SturdyAudioSinkCallback
callbacks.doc: Receives mixed audio from a custom sink. Runs on a thread of the engine's, never the audio thread; `interleaved` holds `frames * channels` floats and is only valid during the call.

callbacks.name: SturdyChunkSystemFn
callbacks.doc:
Body of a system registered with `sturdy_ecs_add_chunk_system_ex` (since 0.35): called once per matching archetype with that archetype's contiguous arrays, instead of once per entity.

`entities` holds `count` entities. `columns[i]` is the first element of an array of `count` components, one array per entry of the access list in the order it was given, each element as large as that component's size; element `r` of every array belongs to `entities[r]`. Write through the arrays declared `STURDY_ACCESS_WRITE`. All pointers are valid only for this call. `commands` is as for `SturdySystemFn`.

One call crosses the language boundary for a whole archetype, so a system over 10,000 entities costs a few calls instead of 10,000: use this for anything per-frame over many entities.

callbacks.name: SturdyEcsVisitFn
callbacks.doc:
Receives one matching entity during `sturdy_ecs_for_each`.

`components` points at an array parallel to the component ids you asked to match, each entry addressing that component's storage for this entity. Write through them to mutate in place. The pointers are valid only for the duration of this call.

While a visit is in progress the world is locked, so this callback must **not** call any other `sturdy_ecs_*` function; each returns `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY`. That guard is doing real work — the engine underneath treats a structural change made during iteration as a fatal contract violation, so without it a reentrant spawn would terminate the process rather than fail. Read and write through `components`; if you need to spawn or destroy, record what you want and do it after `sturdy_ecs_for_each` returns.

callbacks.name: SturdyFileDialogCallback
callbacks.doc: Called once when the dialog closes, possibly on another thread. `paths` holds `count` strings valid only during the call (none when `cancelled`); `filter_index` is the active filter or -1; `error` is null unless the dialog failed.

callbacks.name: SturdyHttpHandlerFn
callbacks.doc: Called for every request, on a handler thread (not the network thread). Call `sturdy_http_respond` exactly once with `responder`, now or later from any thread. A request that is never answered holds its connection until the client gives up.

callbacks.name: SturdyLogCallback
callbacks.doc: Invoked once per log message after registration via `sturdy_log_add_sink`.

callbacks.name: SturdyParChunkFn
callbacks.doc: Body of `sturdy_par_for_chunks`: called with consecutive `[begin, end)` ranges.

callbacks.name: SturdyParForFn
callbacks.doc: Body of `sturdy_par_for`: called once per index, on any worker thread. Must not unwind.

callbacks.name: SturdyParLessFn
callbacks.doc: Returns non-zero when the element at `a` sorts before the one at `b`.

callbacks.name: SturdyParScopeFn
callbacks.doc: Body of `sturdy_par_scope`; `scope` ("par_scope") is valid until `sturdy_par_scope` returns.

callbacks.name: SturdyPluginEntryFn
callbacks.doc: The one function a plugin exports, under the name `sturdy_plugin_entry`. Return `STURDY_OK` to accept the load; anything else aborts it, destroys any modules already added, and `UNLOAD` is *not* called. For `UNLOAD`, `host->context` is valid but `add_module` is refused, and `state` carries what the plugin stored.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionFieldGetFn
callbacks.doc: Same shape as `SturdyReflectionMethodFn`'s two data-access halves — a non-`Trivial` field's copy-out implementation, called with `object` = the field-owning instance.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionFieldSetFn
callbacks.doc: Copy-in counterpart to `SturdyReflectionFieldGetFn`.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionMethodFn
callbacks.doc: A type-erased method call/override/hook body: `object` is the receiver (null for a static method), `args` is one already-typed, caller-marshalled pointer per parameter (see `SturdyReflectionMethodInfo::param_count`), `out_return` is uninitialized storage for the return value (ignored when the method returns nothing), `user_data` is whatever was passed to `sturdy_reflection_register_override`.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionMoveConstructFn
callbacks.doc: Sets the construct/destroy callbacks for the type being built.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionObserverFn
callbacks.doc: A type-erased *observer* body — used for both a method before/after hook and an event listener, which share this exact shape (unlike `SturdyReflectionMethodFn`, there is no `out_return`: neither a hook nor an event listener produces a value, only observes `args`). `object` is the method's receiver (null for a static method) or whatever `sturdy_reflection_fire_event` was called with; `args` is one already-typed pointer per parameter; `user_data` is whatever was passed to `_add_before_hook`/`_add_after_hook`/ `_subscribe_event`.

callbacks.name: SturdyRelayAuthorizeFn
callbacks.doc: Lets the relay authenticate clients. Called on a network thread (answer quickly) with the rendezvous token and the client's address; return non-zero to accept, zero to refuse. `user_data` must stay valid until the relay is released.

callbacks.name: SturdyScriptHostFn
callbacks.doc: A host function: scripts call it by name with a byte string and get a byte string back. Write the result to `result` (or the reason to `error`) and return whether it worked. May be called on any thread a script runs on.

callbacks.name: SturdyStreamFilterMapFn
callbacks.doc: Returns non-zero to emit what was written to `out`, zero to drop the item.

callbacks.name: SturdyStreamPredicateFn
callbacks.doc: Returns non-zero to keep the item.

callbacks.name: SturdyStreamSourceFn
callbacks.doc: Called for each pull on a blocking-lane thread (it may block). Write the next item to `out` and return non-zero, or return zero to end the stream.

callbacks.name: SturdySystemFn
callbacks.doc:
Body of a system registered with `sturdy_ecs_add_system`.

`components` points at an array parallel to the access list the system was registered with, each entry addressing that component's storage for this entity. Write through the ones declared `STURDY_ACCESS_WRITE`; the pointers are valid only for this call.

`commands` queues spawns, destroys and component changes for the engine to apply once the stage finishes. That indirection is not optional — the world cannot be restructured while systems are reading it, which is why the direct `sturdy_ecs_spawn` family reports `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` here.

callbacks.name: SturdyTaskFn
callbacks.doc:
Body of a background task.

Runs on a scheduler worker thread, not the thread that spawned it. Must not unwind.

Nothing in this ABI is safe to call concurrently with the engine's own frame from a worker thread — the ECS and renderer entry points assume the caller is the thread the engine handed a handle to. Use tasks for work that does not touch the engine (loading, decoding, pathfinding, network), publish the result somewhere your game logic reads, and apply it from a system or frame callback.

callbacks.name: SturdyTaskThenFn
callbacks.doc: A later stage of an execution chain: gets the previous stage's result and writes its own (see `sturdy_task_output_set`).

callbacks.name: SturdyTaskWorkFn
callbacks.doc: The work of a task, run on a worker thread. `cancel_token` (a "cancel_token", valid only during the call) turns cancelled when the task's op is cancelled or its join set aborted: poll `sturdy_cancel_token_is_cancelled` to stop early. Fill `output` before returning. Must not unwind.

callbacks.name: SturdyTrayCallback
callbacks.doc: Called on the main thread when a tray menu entry is clicked; `id` is the entry's `id`.

callbacks.name: SturdyWebSocketFn
callbacks.doc: Called for each WebSocket upgraded on a path registered with `sturdy_http_server_on_websocket`, on a handler thread. `socket` is a new "websocket" object **you own** (release it when done; releasing closes the connection). `request` is valid only during the call.

functions.doc:
Reports whether a task has finished.

The non-blocking way to observe one: poll this from your frame callback rather than waiting.

functions.doc:
Reports whether the engine's task scheduler is running.

It starts on first use — the first frame or the first `sturdy_async_spawn` — so this reads false before then.

functions.name: sturdy_async_is_worker_thread
functions.doc:
Reports whether the calling thread is a scheduler worker.

Worth checking before doing anything that blocks: blocking a worker starves the pool it belongs to.

functions.doc: An async mutex / read-write lock protecting a byte-string value. Objects "async_mutex" / "async_rwlock".

Releases a task handle.

functions.name: sturdy_async_rwlock_read

functions.name: sturdy_async_spawn
functions.doc:
Runs `task` on a background thread.

Starts the scheduler if it is not already running.

params.name: task
params.doc: Body to run. Must not be null and must not unwind.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed to `task` untouched. Must stay alive until the task completes, which is not the same as until the handle is released.

params.name: weight

Blocks until a task finishes.

functions.name: sturdy_async_worker_count
functions.doc:
Returns how many worker threads the scheduler has.

Zero when it is not running. Useful for sizing your own work splitting to the machine.

functions.name: sturdy_bloom_settings_init

functions.name: sturdy_broadcast_recv

functions.name: sturdy_broadcast_send

functions.name: sturdy_buffered_shutdown

functions.name: sturdy_buffered_writer_create

functions.doc: "a=1; b=2" for the cookies that apply to a request (string-output convention; empty if none).

functions.name: sturdy_dir_iter_next
functions.doc: Number: 1 and text: the next path, or number 0 at the end.

functions.name: sturdy_display_count
functions.doc: How many monitors are connected (refreshed when the window system reports a change).

functions.name: sturdy_display_mode
functions.doc: Mode `mode_index` (below `SturdyDisplayInfo::mode_count`) of monitor `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_display_name
functions.doc: The monitor's name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_dns_resolve
functions.doc: Resolves a host name. Fields: one `address` per result (numeric text).

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_chunk_system_ex
functions.doc: Registers a chunk system (since 0.35) with a removable handle. Declaration, ordering, conflict detection, `commands` and removal behave exactly as for `sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex`; only the body differs.

params.name: access
params.doc: Components to iterate. At least one is required: a chunk system always iterates, and a system with nothing to iterate belongs on `sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex` as a global system.

params.name: system
params.doc: Body to run. Must not unwind.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_component
functions.doc: Attaches a component to an existing entity.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_PRESENT` if the entity already carries it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_system
functions.doc:
Registers a system that runs every frame, once per entity carrying all the listed components.

The access list is what makes automatic parallelism safe. A C++ system declares its access through its parameter types and the engine derives the rest; a function pointer carries no such information, so you declare it here. The scheduler then orders systems so that nothing writing a component runs alongside anything else touching it, and lets non-conflicting systems run together.

**Declaring less access than you take is the one way to get data races.** If a system might write a component, declare `STURDY_ACCESS_WRITE` even when it usually only reads — an over-declared system costs parallelism, an under-declared one costs correctness.

Systems stay registered for the life of the engine; there is no removal yet.

params.name: access
params.doc: Components the system operates on and how. Must be non-empty, at most 16, and free of duplicates.

params.name: access_count
params.doc: How many entries `access` has.

params.name: system
params.doc: Body to run per entity. Must not unwind.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed through to `system` untouched.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK` once registered. The system first runs on the next frame.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex
functions.doc: Like `sturdy_ecs_add_system_with_resources`, but returns a handle so the system can later be removed, disabled, or ordered. Use this when the system's `user_data` is owned by something that can be destroyed (a script VM, a closure): remove the system first, then free the data.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_system_with_resources
functions.doc:
Registers a system that also touches resources or event channels.

The component half behaves exactly as `sturdy_ecs_add_system`. The resource half is what lets the scheduler order a foreign system against systems — C++ or otherwise — that use the same resources: two systems writing the same resource will not run concurrently, and a reader will not overlap a writer.

Passing zero components registers a **global** system: with nothing to iterate, the body runs exactly once per frame, with a default-constructed entity and a null component array. That is the right shape for a system that only drains an event channel or advances a resource.

params.name: access
params.doc: Components the system operates on. May be null when `access_count` is zero.

params.name: access_count
params.doc: How many entries `access` has. At most 16.

params.name: resource_access
params.doc: Resources and event channels the system operates on. May be null when `resource_access_count` is zero.

params.name: resource_access_count
params.doc: How many entries `resource_access` has.

params.name: system
params.doc: Body to run. Must not unwind.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed through to `system` untouched.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_tag
functions.doc:
Attaches a tag component to an entity.

A convenience over `sturdy_ecs_add_component` that supplies the byte for you, since a tag has no value to pass.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_PRESENT` if the entity already carries it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_clear_events
functions.doc:
Discards every event currently buffered on a channel.

Rarely needed: the engine drains channels once per frame on its own. Use this when a channel is filled and consumed entirely within one frame and should not be seen again.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_add_component
functions.doc: Queues attaching a component, applied after the current stage finishes.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_destroy
functions.doc: Queues destruction of an entity, applied after the current stage finishes.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_remove_component
functions.doc: Queues detaching a component, applied after the current stage finishes.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_spawn
functions.doc: Queues creation of an entity, applied after the current stage finishes.

params.name: commands
params.doc: Handle supplied to your system.

params.name: components
params.doc: Initial value for each component; copied immediately, so your storage need not outlive this call.

params.name: component_count
params.doc: How many entries `components` has.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_field
functions.doc: Reads field `index`, in the order the fields were registered in.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index` is not below `sturdy_ecs_component_field_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_field_count
functions.doc: How many fields a component was registered with (since 0.35); 0 when its registrant did not describe them.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_field_name
functions.doc: Reads field `index`'s name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_info
functions.doc: Reads what the engine knows about a component.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_layout_fingerprint
functions.doc: The 128-bit fingerprint of a component's registered layout (size, alignment, every field's kind, offset and count), as two words; both zero when its registrant did not describe the fields. Lets a binding compare against a value baked in at build time without re-implementing the hash.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_name
functions.doc: Reads a component's canonical name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_event_channel
functions.doc:
Creates an event channel: a buffer of fixed-size records the engine drains every frame.

Events differ from resources in exactly that draining. Anything sent during a frame is readable for the rest of that frame and gone by the next, which is what makes them the right way to communicate between systems without either one owning the data.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name such as `"mygame.damage_event"`.

params.name: event_size
params.doc: Byte size of one event. Must be nonzero.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the channel identifier. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_event_channel_ex
functions.doc:
Like `sturdy_ecs_create_event_channel`, additionally describing the event payload's fields (since 0.35).

An event channel is how two modules written in different languages talk to each other, so they must agree on the payload. `desc->size` is the event size and `align` is ignored. Creating the channel again under the same name must give the same size and, when both calls describe their fields, the same layout (kinds, offsets, counts; names are ignored); a mismatch fails with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and names the first field that differs.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_resource
functions.doc:
Creates a resource, taking ownership of its storage.

The engine's own resources are bound by reference to storage their C++ owner keeps alive. A foreign caller has no comparable place to put that storage, so the engine allocates and owns it here, zero-initialized or copied from `initial_data`. It lives until `sturdy_ecs_destroy_resource` or process exit.

Binding a name that already exists rebinds nothing and succeeds, provided the size matches; a different size under the same name is rejected, because anything already reading it expects the old layout.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name.

params.name: size
params.doc: Byte size. Must be nonzero.

params.name: initial_data
params.doc: Initial value, or null to zero-initialize.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the resource identifier. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_resource_ex
functions.doc: Like `sturdy_ecs_create_resource`, additionally describing the value's fields (since 0.35).

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, `size` and fields, as for `sturdy_ecs_register_component_ex`; `align` is ignored (the engine allocates the storage). Re-creating a resource under the same name must give the same size and, when both calls describe their fields, the same layout: two languages that share a resource must agree on what is in it, not just how big it is. A mismatch fails with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and names the first field that differs.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_destroy
functions.doc: Destroys an entity. Destroying an already-dead entity is a no-op, not an error, so cleanup code does not have to track whether it already ran.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_destroy_resource
functions.doc: Destroys a resource created through `sturdy_ecs_create_resource` and frees its storage.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is bound under that id, or when it is bound to storage this ABI does not own — the engine's own C++ resources cannot be destroyed here.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_event_count
functions.doc: Returns how many events are currently buffered on a channel.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_find_component
functions.doc:
Looks up a component id by canonical name.

Also the way to reach the engine's own components — `"sturdy.engine.world_transform"` and the rest — without registering anything.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is registered under that name.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_for_each
functions.doc:
Visits every live entity carrying all of the listed components.

This is the query primitive: the engine walks only the archetypes that match, so cost scales with matching entities rather than with the whole world.

params.name: components
params.doc: Components an entity must all carry to be visited. At most 16.

params.name: component_count
params.doc: How many entries `components` has.

params.name: visit
params.doc: Invoked once per matching entity. Must not unwind, and must not call back into `sturdy_ecs_*` — see `SturdyEcsVisitFn`.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed through to `visit` untouched.

params.name: out_visited
params.doc: Receives how many entities were visited. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_get_component
functions.doc:
Copies a component's current value out.

A copy rather than a pointer: component storage moves when entities gain or lose components, so a pointer handed across the boundary would go stale in a way the caller could not detect.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size. A mismatch is rejected rather than partially copied, because it means your struct and the engine's disagree.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_get_resource
functions.doc: Copies a resource's current value out.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the resource's byte size.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is bound under that id.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_has_component
functions.doc: Reports whether an entity carries a component. A dead entity reports false rather than failing.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_has_resource
functions.doc: Reports whether a resource is bound.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_is_alive
functions.doc: Reports whether an entity is alive.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_order_system_after
functions.doc: Forces `system` to run in a later stage than `dependency`, in addition to whatever ordering the declared access already implies. A cycle aborts when the schedule is next built.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_read_event
functions.doc: Copies one buffered event out of a channel.

params.name: index
params.doc: Event to read, less than `sturdy_ecs_event_count`.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the channel's event size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_register_component
functions.doc:
Registers a plain-data component type, or returns the existing id if one is already registered under that name.

The component is treated as raw bytes: copied with the equivalent of `memcpy` and destroyed with no cleanup. That is why only plain data works here — a foreign caller has no way to supply C++ construction and destruction semantics, so anything owning a resource must be defined in C++.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name. Use a namespaced form such as `"mygame.health"`; the engine derives a stable key from it, so it must not collide with another component.

params.name: size
params.doc: Bytes per instance. Must be nonzero; use `sturdy_ecs_register_tag_component` for a component that carries no data.

params.name: align
params.doc: Required alignment in bytes. Must be a power of two and at most 64.

params.name: out_component
params.doc: Receives the id.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK`. Re-registering the same name with the same layout returns the original id; re-registering it with a *different* layout is rejected, since existing storage and existing entities are already laid out the old way.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_register_component_ex
functions.doc:
Registers a component and its field layout (since 0.35), so languages sharing it can be checked against each other.

Behaves like `sturdy_ecs_register_component` (same name and layout returns the existing id; a different size or alignment is rejected), and additionally: the fields must fit inside `size` and not overlap, and when this registration and an earlier one of the same name both describe their fields, they must describe the same layout (kinds, offsets, counts; field names are ignored). A mismatch fails with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and a message naming the first field that differs, so a Rust `{f32, f32}` and a C# `{u32, u32}` cannot silently share an 8-byte component. A registration that gives no fields is still accepted against any layout.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_register_tag_component
functions.doc:
Registers a tag component: one that marks an entity without carrying data.

Tags are for querying — "is this entity a player", "is this one asleep" — where the answer is the presence of the component itself. Add and remove them with `sturdy_ecs_add_tag` and `sturdy_ecs_remove_component`, and match them in `sturdy_ecs_for_each` like any other component.

A tag occupies **one byte**, not zero, because that is what an empty struct occupies in C++ and this ABI does not invent a different layout. The pointer a tag yields during iteration is valid but meaningless; there is nothing to read from it.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name.

params.name: out_component
params.doc: Receives the id.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK`. Re-registering an existing tag returns the original id.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_remove_component
functions.doc: Detaches a component from an entity.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_MISSING` if the entity does not carry it, or `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` if it is the entity's last component — destroy the entity instead of emptying it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_remove_system
functions.doc: Unregisters a system. After this returns the engine no longer references its `user_data`. Fails with `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` semantics (a contract violation) if called while a schedule is running, including from inside a system.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_resource_id
functions.doc:
Derives the identifier for a canonical resource or event name.

Pure and engine-independent, so a binding can compute its ids once at load time. The same name always yields the same id, which is what lets a foreign caller name a resource the engine's own C++ code also uses.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name such as `"mygame.score"`.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the identifier.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_set_resource

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_spawn

functions.name: sturdy_engine_key_down

params.name: key

params.name: out_down

functions.name: sturdy_engine_key_just_pressed

functions.name: sturdy_engine_key_just_released

Reads cursor movement accumulated during this tick.

This is the value to integrate for camera look, not the difference between successive `sturdy_engine_mouse_position` reads: it accumulates every motion event the platform delivered this tick, so it stays correct at high polling rates where several events land per frame.

params.name: out_x

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives vertical movement. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_mouse_down

params.name: out_x

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives the vertical position. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_wheel_delta

params.name: out_x
params.doc: Receives horizontal scroll. May be null.

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives vertical scroll. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_exec_just
functions.doc: Lazy descriptions of work that compose and run later (the `Execution` layer). Object "exec_sender"; a sender may be started any number of times. The `user_data` of every stage must stay valid until the sender is released and no run of it is still going.

functions.name: sturdy_exec_submit
functions.doc: Starts the chain. The op carries the last stage's number, bytes and text; cancelling it sets the token every stage receives.

functions.name: sturdy_exec_sync_wait
functions.doc: Starts the chain and blocks for it; `out_op` is a finished op (OK, or failed with the stage's error). Never call it from a worker thread.

functions.name: sturdy_exec_then
functions.doc: A sender that runs `then` on `lane` with the result of `sender`. A failure upstream skips it and propagates.

functions.name: sturdy_file_open
functions.doc: Opens a file for streaming and random access. Object "file". `mode` is a bit set of `SturdyFileMode`. Positional reads and writes use io_uring on Linux when available; nothing occupies a worker thread while the kernel works.

functions.name: sturdy_file_read
functions.doc: Reads up to `max_bytes` at the cursor (advancing it). Bytes: empty at end of file.

functions.name: sturdy_file_read_at
functions.doc: Reads at `offset` without touching the cursor.

functions.name: sturdy_file_read_to_end
functions.doc: Reads from the cursor to the end; fails with `STURDY_IO_INVALID_ARGUMENT` if more than `max_bytes` remain.

functions.name: sturdy_file_seek
functions.doc: Moves the cursor (`origin`: 0 start, 1 current, 2 end). Number: the new position.

functions.name: sturdy_file_size
functions.doc: Number: the size in bytes.

functions.name: sturdy_file_sync
functions.doc: Flushes to stable storage (fsync, or fdatasync when `data_only`).

functions.name: sturdy_file_write
functions.doc: Writes all of `data` at the cursor. Number: bytes written.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_camera_look_at
functions.doc: Points the camera at a world-space target, keeping `+Y` as up.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_ambient_light
functions.doc: Sets uniform ambient radiance and the scene exposure multiplier.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_ambient_occlusion_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the ambient-occlusion stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_anti_aliasing_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the anti-aliasing stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_auto_exposure_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the histogram auto-exposure stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_background_color
functions.doc: Sets the color the scene is cleared to, as linear RGBA.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_bloom_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the bloom stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_emulation_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the camera-emulation stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_perspective
functions.doc: Sets a perspective projection.

params.name: near_clip

params.name: far_clip
params.doc: Far plane distance.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_position
functions.doc: Places the camera at a world-space position.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_viewport
functions.doc:
Sets the camera's aspect ratio from a viewport size in pixels.

Pass the `framebuffer_width`/`framebuffer_height` from this frame's `SturdyFrameInput` unless you are deliberately rendering at a different aspect. Both must be nonzero.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_color_grade_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the colour-grade settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_debug_label
functions.doc: Attaches a debug label to this frame, surfaced in graphics debuggers and engine logs.

params.name: label
params.doc: Null-terminated UTF-8, or null to clear. Copied; need not outlive the call.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_depth_of_field_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the depth-of-field settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_feature_enabled
functions.doc: Enables or disables one render-graph stage for this frame.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_lighting_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the clustered-lighting settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_motion_blur_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the motion-blur stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_reflection_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the reflection settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_resolution_scale
functions.doc: Scales the internal render resolution relative to the surface. Must be in (0, 2].
