functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_restir_gi_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the ReSTIR GI stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_scene_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the scene stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_screen_space_gi_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the screen-space GI stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_shadow_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the shadow stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_tone_mapping
functions.doc: Selects the tone-mapping operator and its exposure/white-point/saturation controls.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_tone_mapping_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the tone-mapping stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_volumetric_fog_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the volumetric-fog settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_framed_create
functions.doc: Messages over a byte stream. `io` must read and write ("tcp", "file", "pipe_end"). `max_frame_bytes` 0: 8 MiB (64 KiB for lines). Object "framed".

functions.name: sturdy_framed_next
functions.doc: Number 1 and bytes: the next frame; number 0 at a clean end of stream.

functions.name: sturdy_framed_stream
functions.doc: The remaining frames as a "stream" object (do not call `sturdy_framed_next` meanwhile).

functions.name: sturdy_frames_count
functions.doc: How many frames `packed` holds; `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when it is malformed.

functions.name: sturdy_frames_get
functions.doc: Frame `index` (bytes-output convention).

functions.name: sturdy_frames_pack
functions.doc: Several byte strings in one: a 32-bit little-endian count, then each as a 32-bit little-endian length and its bytes. Used where an operation or stream item carries more than one value. Packs `count` views (bytes-output convention: null buffer to learn the size).

functions.name: sturdy_fs_exists
functions.doc: Number: 1 if the path exists, else 0.

functions.name: sturdy_fs_list
functions.doc: Entry paths of a directory. Bytes: the paths as packed frames (`sturdy_frames_count` / `sturdy_frames_get`). Number: how many. At most `max_entries` (0: 4096); more fail with `STURDY_IO_INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

functions.name: sturdy_fs_read_file
functions.doc: Reads a whole file on the IO lane. Bytes: the content; `STURDY_IO_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when it is larger than `max_bytes` (0: unlimited).

functions.name: sturdy_fs_read_range
functions.doc: Reads `byte_count` bytes at `offset` (fewer at the end of the file). Bytes: the content.

functions.name: sturdy_fs_remove_directory
functions.doc: Removes a directory and everything in it. Number: 1 if something was removed.

functions.name: sturdy_fs_remove_file
functions.doc: Number: 1 if something was removed.

functions.name: sturdy_fs_size
functions.doc: Number: the size in bytes.

functions.name: sturdy_fs_write_file
functions.doc: Creates or replaces the file with `data`, or appends to it.

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_count
functions.doc: How many devices are connected (also starts the joystick subsystem on first use).

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_name
functions.doc: The device's name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_raw_counts
functions.doc: How many axes, buttons and hats a device reports raw.

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_raw_read
functions.doc: A device as the hardware reports it. Each buffer may be null; axes are -1 to 1, buttons 0/1, hats a bit set (1 up, 2 right, 4 down, 8 left).

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_rumble
functions.doc: Motor strengths are 0..1; the rumble stops after `duration_ms`.

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_sensor
functions.doc: x, y, z of an enabled sensor (m/s^2 for the accelerometer, rad/s for the gyroscope).

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_state
functions.doc: The current state of a mapped gamepad (`STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` for an unknown or unmapped device).

functions.name: sturdy_gamepad_take_events
functions.doc: Devices connected or disconnected since the last call: writes up to `capacity` events and sets `*out_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_import
functions.doc:
Imports a glTF or GLB file, creating a model asset for every mesh it contains.

Importing does not put anything in the world — it produces assets and a description of how the file arranged them. Call `sturdy_gltf_spawn_all` to reproduce that arrangement, or walk the instances yourself if you want to filter or re-place them.

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to a `.gltf` or `.glb` file. A `.gltf` referencing external buffers and images resolves them relative to its own directory, so move the whole folder together.

params.name: shader
params.doc: Shader every imported model draws with. Load one with `sturdy_render_load_shader`.

params.name: out_scene
params.doc: Receives the scene handle. Release it with `sturdy_gltf_release`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_instance_at
functions.doc: Reads the node instance at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_instance_count
functions.doc: Returns how many node instances the scene places.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_instance_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of the node instance at `index`. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_light_at
functions.doc: Reads the light at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_light_count
functions.doc: Returns how many lights the scene declares.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_light_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of the light at `index`. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_model_at
functions.doc: Reads the model asset at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_model_count
functions.doc: Returns how many distinct models the import produced.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_release
functions.doc:
Releases an imported scene.

Frees the instance and light lists this ABI is holding. The model assets survive — they belong to the asset manager — so anything already spawned keeps rendering.

Releasing twice reports `STURDY_ERROR_HANDLE_EXPIRED` rather than corrupting anything, since scene tokens are never reused.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_spawn_all
functions.doc:
Spawns an entity for every instance and light in the scene, reproducing it as authored.

The convenience path: import, spawn, release. Instances with no model are skipped, since an entity that draws nothing and lights nothing would only cost iteration.

params.name: out_spawned
params.doc: Receives how many entities were created. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_gpu_enumerate
functions.doc: Enumerates every physical GPU this machine can create an engine on, across every graphics backend this build supports. Safe to call before `sturdy_runtime_run`, with no window or device yet — this is how an application builds its own GPU picker rather than guessing at `physical_device_id` values. Not free: it creates and immediately destroys a temporary graphics instance per backend, so call it once and cache the result rather than every frame.

params.name: out_gpus
params.doc: Copies up to `capacity` entries here.

params.name: capacity
params.doc: Size of `out_gpus`, in entries. May be 0 to just read `*out_count`.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives the true number of GPUs found, which may exceed `capacity` — realistically never more than a handful, so a generously sized buffer (8) avoids this.

functions.name: sturdy_guard_get
functions.doc: The protected value (bytes-output convention).

functions.name: sturdy_guard_release
functions.doc: Unlocks now.

functions.name: sturdy_guard_set
functions.doc: Replaces the value (mutex and write guards only).

functions.name: sturdy_http_body_closed
functions.doc: Finishes when the client disconnected or the server stopped, so a producer can stop. Cancelling it finishes it as cancelled.

functions.name: sturdy_http_body_finish
functions.doc: Ends the body once queued chunks drain.

functions.name: sturdy_http_body_write
functions.doc: Queues a chunk. Finishes once it is accepted into the bounded queue (so a slow client paces the producer); fails with `STURDY_IO_CLOSED` once the client is gone or the body was finished.

functions.name: sturdy_http_client_close_idle
functions.doc: Closes idle pooled connections.

functions.name: sturdy_http_client_cookie_jar
functions.doc: The jar a client uses (shared, not a copy). `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when cookies are off.

functions.name: sturdy_http_client_create
functions.doc: Creates a client with a connection pool (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, HTTP/2 multiplexing, HTTP/3 after `Alt-Svc`). Object "http_client".

functions.name: sturdy_http_client_request
functions.doc: Sends a request. Number: status. Fields: the response headers. Bytes: the body. Text: the final URL after redirects. Non-2xx statuses are ordinary results; only transport, TLS, protocol, limit and timeout problems fail the op. `X-` headers etc. are yours; `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Connection` and `Transfer-Encoding` are managed by the client and ignored if supplied.

functions.name: sturdy_http_format_sse
functions.doc: The wire format of one event, ending with the blank line that dispatches it (string-output convention).

functions.name: sturdy_http_percent_decode
functions.doc: Percent-decodes `text` (string-output convention); `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on a malformed escape or an encoded NUL.

functions.name: sturdy_http_respond
functions.doc: Sends the response for a request. `headers` may be null. CR/LF in a header makes the server answer 500 instead.

functions.name: sturdy_http_respond_canned
functions.doc: Sends a canned response of `kind` with `status` (a redirect usually 302/301/307/308) and the null-terminated `body`.

functions.name: sturdy_http_respond_ex
functions.doc: Sends a response. Fails (without spending `responder`) with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` if more than one body is given. For `stream` or `sse` responses `out_body` receives the writer object (required then); otherwise it is ignored and may be null. The writer is yours to release; releasing it ends the body.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_begin
functions.doc: Opens the listener and starts serving.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_create
functions.doc: Creates a server without starting it, so WebSocket paths can be added first; `sturdy_http_server_begin` then starts it. Object "http_server". `handler` answers every request that is not a WebSocket upgrade.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_create_router
functions.doc: Same, serving a router (see below). The router may be released afterwards: the server keeps an immutable snapshot of it.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_http3_port
functions.doc: 0 when HTTP/3 is not served.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_info
functions.doc: Static server facts as a finished op's fields: `running`, `tls`, `http2` ("1"/"0"), `port`, `http3_port`.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_metrics
functions.doc: Counters as a finished op's fields (decimal text): connections_accepted, requests, responses_2xx..5xx, active_connections, ...

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_on_websocket
functions.doc: Upgrades requests whose path (without query) equals `path` to WebSockets, on the same port and over TLS when the server uses it. Call before `sturdy_http_server_begin`. `user_data` must stay valid until the server object is released.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_start
functions.doc: Starts an HTTP(S) server. Object "http_server". Stops (and drains) when the object is released.

functions.name: sturdy_http_server_start_router
functions.doc: `sturdy_http_server_create_router` and `sturdy_http_server_begin` in one step.

functions.name: sturdy_input_gamepad_event_count
functions.doc: Pads plugged or unplugged since the previous tick.

functions.name: sturdy_input_set_gamepads_enabled
functions.doc: Starts (or stops) sampling gamepads every tick. Off by default.

functions.name: sturdy_interval_create
functions.doc: A periodic timer that does not drift. Object "interval"; `sturdy_interval_tick` finishes at each period boundary.

functions.name: sturdy_io_copy
functions.doc: Copies until the reader ends, overlapping each read with the previous write. Number: bytes copied.

functions.name: sturdy_io_lane_configure
functions.doc: Tunes the blocking-IO lane (0 workers: automatic; 0 `max_pending`: 1024). `out_applied` says whether it took effect (false once it started).

functions.name: sturdy_io_lane_stats
functions.doc: Fields `backend`, `workers`, `pending`, `capacity` (a finished op).

functions.name: sturdy_io_read_to_end
functions.doc: Bytes: everything until the reader ends; `STURDY_IO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` past `max_bytes` (0: unlimited).

functions.name: sturdy_join_set_abort_all
functions.doc: Sets the cancel token of every running task in the set.

functions.name: sturdy_join_set_create
functions.doc: A dynamic set of tasks joined in completion order. Object "join_set".

functions.name: sturdy_join_set_join_next
functions.doc: Finishes with the next task to complete. Field `outcome` is "ok", "failed" (field `error` says why) or "empty" (nothing left); number, bytes and text are the task's.

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_message
functions.doc: Detail for the most recent failing call **on the calling thread**.
functions.returns: A null-terminated UTF-8 string, never null; empty when the last call succeeded. The pointer stays valid until the next ABI call on this same thread, so copy it if you need to keep it. Never freed by the caller.
notes: Thread-local by design: engine frames can run on their own render threads, so a process-wide error slot would let one thread's failure overwrite another's.

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_trace_format
functions.doc: The whole trace as readable text, one frame per line, with the usual size-query convention (see `copy_string_out` in the ABI notes: pass a null buffer to learn the size; a short buffer gets a truncated, terminated result and `STURDY_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`).

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_trace_frame
functions.doc: Reads one frame of the trace counted by `sturdy_last_error_trace_frame_count`, innermost first.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index` is past the end.

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_trace_frame_count
functions.doc: Number of frames in the calling thread's most recent trace (the last failure's, or the last `sturdy_trace_capture`). Zero if none. Call this before `sturdy_last_error_trace_frame`: it resolves the trace once so the frames can be read cheaply.

functions.name: sturdy_lighting_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (clustered on).

functions.name: sturdy_local_set_block_on
functions.doc: Runs queued tasks on the calling thread until `op` finishes (blocks).

functions.name: sturdy_local_set_create
functions.doc: Tasks that run only on the thread that pumps the set. Object "local_set".

functions.name: sturdy_local_set_run_pending
functions.doc: Runs queued tasks on the calling thread until none are left. `out_ran` (may be null): how many.

functions.name: sturdy_log_add_sink
functions.doc: Registers a callback to receive every subsequent log message.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Function invoked per message. Must not be null.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Opaque pointer passed back to `callback` unchanged. May be null.

params.name: out_sink
params.doc: Receives a handle to unregister this sink later with `sturdy_log_remove_sink`.

functions.name: sturdy_log_remove_sink
functions.doc: Unregisters a sink added by `sturdy_log_add_sink`. A null/zero handle, or one already removed, is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_main_thread_pump
functions.doc: Runs the queued main-thread work on the calling thread.

functions.name: sturdy_main_thread_run
functions.doc: Queues `fn` for the engine's main thread (run when it pumps). `user_data` must stay valid until `fn` has run.

functions.name: sturdy_main_thread_set_wake_hook
functions.doc: Installs a callback run (on the posting thread) after every queued job, so a loop that blocks waiting for events can wake and pump. Null removes it.

functions.name: sturdy_memory_pipe_create
functions.doc: Two connected in-memory ends ("pipe_end"): what one writes the other reads. `chunks`: messages buffered per direction (0: 8).

functions.name: sturdy_memory_reader_create
functions.doc: A reader over a copy of `data`. Object "memory_reader".

functions.name: sturdy_memory_writer_create
functions.doc: A writer that collects what it is given. Object "memory_writer".

functions.name: sturdy_model_import
functions.doc: Imports a model file of any supported format, chosen from its extension: `.gltf`/`.glb`, `.fbx`, `.obj`. Same ownership and release rules as `sturdy_gltf_import`; the handle works with every `sturdy_gltf_*` call.

functions.name: sturdy_module_count
functions.doc: How many modules are loaded.

functions.name: sturdy_module_name
functions.doc: The name of the module at `index` in start order. See the string-output convention above.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index` is not below `sturdy_module_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_module_request_load
functions.doc: Adds and starts a module in the running game, after the modules in `module->after` (which must already be loaded).

functions.name: sturdy_module_request_reload
functions.doc: Replaces the module called `name` with `logic`, in the same place in the start order and with the same options. The old module is shut down and its registrations removed first. If `logic`'s `on_engine_initialized` returns false the module stays unloaded and the failure is reported.

functions.name: sturdy_module_request_unload
functions.doc: Unloads a module: its `on_shutdown` runs, what it registered is removed, and it is destroyed. Refused when another module names it in `after`. Returns `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the game was not started with `sturdy_runtime_run_modules`.

functions.name: sturdy_module_take_failure
functions.doc: Takes the oldest message of a live change that failed, copying it out (see the string-output convention above); it is removed only when the copy succeeded, so a too-small buffer can be retried.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when no change has failed since the last call drained them.

functions.name: sturdy_motion_blur_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (disabled — motion blur is opt-in).

functions.name: sturdy_nat_default_gateway
functions.doc: The default gateway's address ("" when it cannot be determined).

functions.name: sturdy_nat_map_port
functions.doc: Asks the router to forward a public port to this machine (PCP, NAT-PMP or UPnP IGD). Object "mapping". Number: granted lifetime in seconds (0: permanent — remove it yourself). Fields: external_host, external_port, method, gateway. Renew before half the lifetime.

functions.name: sturdy_nat_punch_hole
functions.doc: UDP hole punching: both peers call this at once with the other's candidate addresses ("host:port") and a shared secret. Text/number: the candidate that answered; keep using the same socket afterwards. Fails with `STURDY_IO_TIMED_OUT` (typical of symmetric NATs: use a relay).

functions.name: sturdy_nat_unmap_port
functions.doc: Removes a mapping made by `sturdy_nat_map_port`.

functions.name: sturdy_native_available
functions.doc:
Reports whether raw native handles are available.

False when `SturdyRuntimeConfig::enable_native_access` was not set, or when the backend could not publish them. Check this before calling the getters below rather than treating their failure as fatal.

functions.name: sturdy_native_d3d12
functions.doc: Reads the engine's raw D3D12 objects.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the active backend is not D3D12, or when native access was not enabled.

functions.name: sturdy_native_d3d12_queue
functions.doc: Reads the `ID3D12CommandQueue *` backing one queue lane.

params.name: queue_class
params.doc: Class of queue to resolve.

params.name: lane_index
params.doc: Lane within that class.

params.name: out_queue
params.doc: Receives the queue. Must not be null. Not `AddRef`'d.

functions.name: sturdy_native_vulkan
functions.doc: Reads the engine's raw Vulkan objects.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the active backend is not Vulkan, or when native access was not enabled.

functions.name: sturdy_native_vulkan_queue
functions.doc: Reads the `VkQueue` and queue family index backing one queue lane.

params.name: queue_class
params.doc: Class of queue to resolve.

params.name: lane_index
params.doc: Lane within that class.

params.name: out_queue
params.doc: Receives the `VkQueue`. May be null.

params.name: out_queue_family_index
params.doc: Receives the Vulkan queue family index, which is what you need to create your own command pool against this queue. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_native_webgpu
functions.doc: Reads the engine's raw WebGPU objects.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the active backend is not WebGPU, or when native access was not enabled.

functions.name: sturdy_network_reactor_configure
functions.doc: Sets the number of network reactor threads. `out_applied` says whether it took effect (false once the reactor is running).

functions.name: sturdy_notify_create
functions.doc: A wake-up signal with at most one stored permit. Object "notify".

functions.name: sturdy_notify_notified
functions.doc: Finishes when notified; a `sturdy_notify_one` that happened earlier with nobody waiting is consumed first.

functions.name: sturdy_object_kind
functions.doc: The object's kind ("tcp", "websocket", "quic_stream", ...), following the string-output convention.

functions.name: sturdy_object_release
functions.doc: Releases an object, closing whatever it wraps. Operations still pending on it finish as closed or cancelled.

functions.name: sturdy_oneshot_create
functions.doc: One-shot value hand-off. Objects "oneshot_sender" / "oneshot_receiver". A sender released without sending fails the receiver with `STURDY_IO_CLOSED`.

functions.name: sturdy_oneshot_recv
functions.doc: Bytes: the value. A receiver can be waited on once.

functions.name: sturdy_oneshot_send
functions.doc: `out_first` (may be null) says whether this call set the value.

functions.name: sturdy_op_bytes
functions.doc: The result's bytes. Pass a null buffer to learn the size; `out_length` always receives the full size, and `STURDY_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` is returned (after copying what fits) when the buffer was smaller. No terminator is added.

functions.name: sturdy_op_cancel
functions.doc: Asks the operation to stop. It then finishes as `STURDY_OP_CANCELLED` (or with its result, if it already had one). Harmless on a finished op.

functions.name: sturdy_op_error_code
functions.doc: The failure kind of a `STURDY_OP_FAILED` op (`STURDY_IO_NONE` otherwise). `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` while pending.

functions.name: sturdy_op_error_message
functions.doc: The failure message of a failed op (empty otherwise), following the string-output convention.

functions.name: sturdy_op_field
functions.doc: Value of the first field called `name` (HTTP header lookup is case-insensitive; other fields are exact). `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when there is none.

functions.name: sturdy_op_field_count
functions.doc: How many named fields the result has.

functions.name: sturdy_op_field_name
functions.doc: Name of field `index`, following the string-output convention.

functions.name: sturdy_op_field_value
functions.doc: Value of field `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_op_link_cancel
functions.doc: Cancelling `token` cancels `op`.

functions.name: sturdy_op_number
functions.doc: The result's number (byte count, status code, port, ... — see the function that made the op).

functions.name: sturdy_op_object
functions.doc: The object the operation produced (a connection, a file, ...), as a new handle you own. Calling it again returns the same handle. `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the op produced none. The object lives until **both** its handle and the operation are released, so a "permit" or a "mutex_guard" is only dropped once the op is released too — or release it explicitly with its own function.

functions.name: sturdy_op_on_complete
functions.doc: Runs `callback` when the operation finishes — at once, on this thread, if it already has.

functions.name: sturdy_op_ready
functions.doc: An already-finished op (Tokio's `ready`): useful to answer an operation-shaped API without work.

functions.name: sturdy_op_release
functions.doc: Releases an operation. A pending one keeps running; its result is dropped.

functions.name: sturdy_op_status
functions.doc: Reads an operation's status without blocking.

functions.name: sturdy_op_text
functions.doc: The result's text, following the string-output convention.

functions.name: sturdy_op_wait
functions.doc: Waits until the operation finishes or `timeout_ms` passes (negative: no limit). `out_done` says which. Blocks the calling thread; do not call it from a completion callback.

functions.name: sturdy_op_wait_any
functions.doc: Waits for the first of `ops` to finish. `out_index` is its position, or -1 when `timeout_ms` passed first.

functions.name: sturdy_op_with_timeout
functions.doc: A new op that finishes as `op` does, or fails with `STURDY_IO_TIMED_OUT` after `timeout_ms` — cancelling `op` then. Cancelling the new op cancels `op`.

functions.name: sturdy_par_any
functions.doc: Parallel predicates over `[0, count)`.

functions.name: sturdy_par_find_first
functions.doc: The lowest index for which `pred` holds (-1: none) / any such index.

functions.name: sturdy_par_for
functions.doc: Runs `body` for every index in `[0, count)` across the worker pool and returns when all are done (the caller helps, so it never deadlocks the pool). `min_chunk` is the smallest run of indices handed to one task (0/1: let the engine decide). Calling it from inside a body is fine.

functions.name: sturdy_par_for_chunks
functions.doc: Runs `body` over consecutive ranges of at most `chunk` indices (`chunk` must be positive).

functions.name: sturdy_par_for_windows
functions.doc: Calls `body(begin)` for every window start in `[0, count - window]`.

functions.name: sturdy_par_join
functions.doc: Runs `a` and `b` in parallel and returns when both are done.

functions.name: sturdy_par_map_reduce_i64
functions.doc: Maps every index and combines the results with an associative `reduce` that has `identity`.

functions.name: sturdy_par_min_max_f32
functions.doc: Parallel minimum and maximum. `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `count` is 0.

functions.name: sturdy_par_num_threads
functions.doc: The threads a parallel call can use right now.

functions.name: sturdy_par_reduce
functions.doc: Reduces a typed array in parallel. `out_has_value` is false for an empty array with min/max.

functions.name: sturdy_par_scope
functions.doc: Runs `body` with a scope; every task spawned on the scope finishes before this returns.

functions.name: sturdy_par_sort
functions.doc: Sorts `count` elements of `type` in place, ascending, in parallel.

functions.name: sturdy_par_sort_by
functions.doc: Sorts `count` elements of `element_size` bytes in place with `less`; `stable` keeps equal elements in order.

functions.name: sturdy_par_sum_f32
functions.doc: Parallel sums. Float sums use SIMD and may differ from a sequential sum by rounding.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_block
functions.doc: Refuses the peer from now on and drops it if connected.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_broadcast
functions.doc: Sends to every connected peer, except `except_peer_id` when non-null (forwarding what that peer just sent). Number: how many links took it.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_connect
functions.doc: Dials a peer. `expected_id` non-null pins it (the link is refused if someone else answers). Fields of the linked peer: id, name, address, inbound, listen_port.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_connect_via_relay
functions.doc: Meets a peer through a relay when neither can be dialed. Both sides use the same `token` and opposite `dial`; the peer-to-peer TLS runs through the relay end to end. `relay_tls` non-null: the hop to the relay itself uses TLS too.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_disconnect
functions.doc: Drops a peer; `reason` (null: "disconnected by application") is what the other side sees.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_identity
functions.doc: The node's identity as a finished op: fields `certificate_pem`, `private_key_pem`, `sha256`. Persist it to keep the same id.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_list
functions.doc: Connected peers as a finished op: fields `id:N`, `name:N`, `address:N`, `inbound:N`, `listen_port:N` for N = 0, 1, ...

functions.name: sturdy_peer_next_event
functions.doc: Next event. Number: 0 connected, 1 disconnected, 2 message, 3 discovered. Bytes: the message. Fields: peer, channel, name, address, reason, inbound. Not consuming events eventually stalls the peers' readers.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_send
functions.doc: Sends a message on channel 0..0xFEFF to one peer.

functions.name: sturdy_peer_start
functions.doc: Starts a peer node: encrypted, mutually authenticated links with self-certifying ids. Object "peer"; text: our peer id.

functions.name: sturdy_permit_forget
functions.doc: Keeps the permits consumed forever (they are never returned).

functions.name: sturdy_permit_release
functions.doc: Returns the permits now.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_language
functions.doc: The language the plugin reported through `set_info`, empty when it did not. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_load
functions.doc: Opens a plugin library and runs its entry point with `STURDY_PLUGIN_LOAD`, collecting its modules (nothing is started).
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the library cannot be opened or exports no `sturdy_plugin_entry` (the cause is in the error message); `STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` when the entry point refuses; the entry point's own error otherwise.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_module_count
functions.doc: How many modules the plugin added.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_module_name
functions.doc: The name of module `index`, in the order the plugin added them.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_name
functions.doc: The plugin's reported name (falls back to the file name).

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_release
functions.doc: Releases the caller's handle. The library closes once every module that was handed out has been destroyed (immediately when none was). Modules that were never handed out are destroyed now.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_request_load
functions.doc: Adds every module of the plugin to the running game (as `sturdy_module_request_load` for each, in the order added). Consumes the plugin's modules like `sturdy_plugin_take_modules`.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_request_reload
functions.doc: Replaces `previous`'s modules with `next`'s in the running game: same-named modules are reloaded in place, new ones are loaded, and names `previous` had that `next` lacks are unloaded. Consumes `next`'s modules. Release `previous` afterwards; its library closes when its modules are gone.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_request_unload
functions.doc: Unloads every module of `plugin` from the running game. Release the handle afterwards.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_take_modules
functions.doc: Hands the plugin's modules to the caller, to pass to `sturdy_runtime_run_modules` (the returned strings and arrays stay valid until `sturdy_plugin_release`). Each module's ownership moves to whatever consumes it, so this works once per plugin: a second call returns `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY`. If `capacity` is smaller than the module count, `STURDY_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` is returned and nothing is handed out; `out_count` always receives the count.

functions.name: sturdy_pool_create
functions.doc: Creates a separate worker pool (Rayon's `ThreadPoolBuilder`): work run through it stays on its own threads, so a long job cannot starve the engine's scheduler. `threads` 0: the machine's core count. Object "pool"; released objects shut their threads down.

functions.name: sturdy_pool_par_for
functions.doc: `sturdy_par_for` on the pool's own threads.

functions.name: sturdy_pool_run
functions.doc: Runs `task` on the pool and waits for it (anything it parallelises stays on the pool).

functions.name: sturdy_presentation_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and the engine's defaults (vsync on, no HDR, opaque composition, automatic image count).

functions.name: sturdy_process_read_stdout
functions.doc: Bytes: up to `max_bytes` from the child's stdout / stderr (empty at end).

functions.name: sturdy_process_request_exit
functions.doc: Asks the child to exit (SIGTERM / a close request); `sturdy_process_kill` forces it.

functions.name: sturdy_process_run
functions.doc: Runs a program to completion, feeding `stdin_data` and collecting stdout/stderr (bounded; the child is killed past `max_output_bytes` — 0: 16 MiB — or `timeout_ms` — 0: no limit). Bytes: stdout. Text: stderr. Number: exit code (the signal number if signalled). Fields: `signaled`, `success`.

functions.name: sturdy_process_spawn
functions.doc: Starts a child (standard streams per the options, piped by default). Object "process".

functions.name: sturdy_process_wait
functions.doc: Number: exit code (the signal number if signalled). Fields: `signaled`, `success`, `signal`.

functions.name: sturdy_promise_cancel
functions.doc: Completes the future as cancelled.

functions.name: sturdy_promise_create
functions.doc: The producing half of an operation: something other than the engine finishes `out_future` by calling `sturdy_promise_set_*`. Object "promise"; `out_future` is an ordinary op (wait on it, attach a callback, link or time it out). Only the first completion wins; a promise released while pending fails its future with `STURDY_IO_CLOSED`.

functions.name: sturdy_promise_set_value
functions.doc: Completes the future with a number, bytes and text. `out_first` (may be null) says whether this call completed it.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_accept
functions.doc: Next connection whose handshake completed. Object "quic_conn".

functions.name: sturdy_quic_accept_stream
functions.doc: Next stream the peer opened. Object "quic_stream".

functions.name: sturdy_quic_close
functions.doc: Closes the connection with an application error code (0 = clean).

functions.name: sturdy_quic_closed
functions.doc: Finishes when the connection ends, for any reason. Number: the code. Text: the reason. Fields: `from_peer`, `application`, `timed_out` ("1"/"0").

functions.name: sturdy_quic_connect
functions.doc: Connects and completes the TLS 1.3 handshake. Object "quic_conn". Datagrams and many streams, no head-of-line blocking.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_info
functions.doc: Fields: `peer`, `local`, and once the handshake finished `protocol`, `alpn`, `peer_sha256`, `cipher` (a finished op).

functions.name: sturdy_quic_listen
functions.doc: Starts a QUIC server. Object "quic_listener" (finished op).

functions.name: sturdy_quic_listener_metrics
functions.doc: Counters as a finished op's fields: connections_accepted, retries_sent, rejected_limit, ...

functions.name: sturdy_quic_open_stream
functions.doc: Opens a stream (waits if the peer's stream limit is reached). Object "quic_stream".

functions.name: sturdy_quic_receive_datagram
functions.doc: Next received datagram. Bytes: the payload.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_send_datagram
functions.doc: Sends one unreliable datagram; it may be lost or reordered. `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when larger than the current maximum, `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` when the send queue is full, `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the peer takes no datagrams.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_stats
functions.doc: Fields (decimal): rtt_us, min_rtt_us, bytes_in_flight, cwnd, packets_lost, bytes_sent, bytes_received (a finished op).

functions.name: sturdy_quic_stream_finish
functions.doc: Ends the sending side cleanly after everything queued.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_stream_receive
functions.doc: 1..`max_bytes` bytes as they arrive. Bytes: empty means the peer finished. Reading is what grants the peer more credit.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_stream_reset
functions.doc: Abruptly stops sending (the peer's reads fail with `error_code`) / asks the peer to stop sending.

functions.name: sturdy_quic_stream_send
functions.doc: Queues data on a stream; finishes once it fits under `stream_send_buffer` (so a slow peer paces the sender).

functions.name: sturdy_rate_limiter_create
functions.doc: A keyed token bucket: each key may use `rate_per_second` operations per second on average, with bursts up to `burst`. Thread-safe; memory is bounded by `max_keys` (0: 10000). Object "rate_limiter".

functions.name: sturdy_rate_limiter_retry_after_ms
functions.doc: Milliseconds until `key` could take `cost` tokens (0 if it could now).

functions.name: sturdy_rate_limiter_try_acquire
functions.doc: Takes `cost` tokens for `key` if available.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_add_after_hook
functions.doc: Adds a listener that fires just after a method returns. See `sturdy_reflection_add_before_hook`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_add_before_hook
functions.doc: Adds a listener that fires just before a method runs (with the same `args` the real call receives), in addition to — not instead of — the real implementation/override. Unlike `sturdy_reflection_register_override`, any number of mods may add hooks without clobbering each other's.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_clear_override
functions.doc: Removes a previously installed override, restoring the real implementation.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_get_element
functions.doc: Reads the element at `index` out of a container field.

params.name: element_size
params.doc: Must equal the container's declared element size.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index >= sturdy_reflection_container_size(...)`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_resize
functions.doc: Resizes a container field to exactly `new_size` elements (default-constructing new ones, destroying truncated ones).
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the element type has no default constructor.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_set_element
functions.doc: Writes `data` into the element at `index` of a container field. See `sturdy_reflection_container_get_element`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_size
functions.doc: Returns a container field's current element count.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_field_info
functions.doc: Reads what the engine knows about a field.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_event
functions.doc: Looks up a declared hook point by name, walking `type`'s reflected base chain. See `sturdy_reflection_find_field`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_field
functions.doc: Looks up a field by name, walking `type`'s reflected base chain if not declared directly on it (the same behavior as `TypeRegistry::find_field`).
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when no such field is declared on `type` or any ancestor.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_method
functions.doc: Looks up a method by name, walking `type`'s reflected base chain. See `sturdy_reflection_find_field`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_type
functions.doc: Looks up a reflected type by canonical name.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is registered under that name.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_fire_event
functions.doc: Fires an event, calling every subscribed listener in registration order. A no-op — cheap, no error — when nobody has subscribed.

params.name: args
params.doc: One already-typed pointer per event parameter. Pass null when the event takes none.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_get_field
functions.doc: Copies a field's current value out of `object` into `out_data`.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the field's registered size (`SturdyReflectionFieldInfo::size`) — a mismatch is rejected rather than partially copied.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on a size mismatch or a field with no readable representation (an opaque non-`Trivial`, non-container field this ABI cannot copy).

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_get_static_field
functions.doc: Copies a static field's current value out. There is no per-instance object — the field has one true address, tracked internally.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_invoke_method
functions.doc: Calls an instance method on `object`, dispatching to a mod-installed override (`sturdy_reflection_register_override`) instead of the real implementation when one is present, and firing any before/after hooks around it either way.

params.name: args
params.doc: One already-typed pointer per parameter, in declared order (`SturdyReflectionMethodInfo::param_count` entries). Pass null when `param_count` is 0.

params.name: out_return
params.doc: Receives the return value (`out_return_size` bytes), ignored when the method returns nothing. May be null if you do not need it.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when `arg_count` does not match `param_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_invoke_static_method
functions.doc: Calls a static method. See `sturdy_reflection_invoke_method`; there is no receiver.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_method_info
functions.doc: Reads what the engine knows about a method.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_register_override
functions.doc: Installs a full replacement for a method — `sturdy_reflection_invoke_method`/ `_invoke_static_method` call `override_fn` instead of the real implementation from this point on. Only one override may be active per method; installing a second silently replaces the first (there is no chain — a mod that wants "wrap, not replace" should call through the before/after hooks instead, or capture and call the previous override itself before installing its own).

params.name: override_fn
params.doc: Must not be null. Pass a null-checking no-op and call `sturdy_reflection_clear_override` instead of passing null here to remove an override.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_remove_after_hook
functions.doc: Removes a hook added by `sturdy_reflection_add_after_hook`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_remove_before_hook
functions.doc: Removes a hook added by `sturdy_reflection_add_before_hook`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_set_field
functions.doc: Overwrites a field's value in place on `object`. See `sturdy_reflection_get_field`.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on a size mismatch, a `ReadOnly` field, or a field with no writable representation.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_set_static_field
functions.doc: Overwrites a static field's value. See `sturdy_reflection_get_static_field`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_subscribe_event
functions.doc: Subscribes a listener to a declared hook point (`SFT_REFLECT_EVENT`). Any number of mods may subscribe to the same event independently.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_add_event
functions.doc: Declares one hook point on the type being built. See `SFT_REFLECT_EVENT`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_add_field
functions.doc: Declares one field on the type being built.

params.name: is_trivial
params.doc: True when raw offset+memcpy access is safe (`copy_get`/`copy_set` are then ignored and may be null); false requires both callbacks.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_add_method
functions.doc: Declares one method on the type being built.

params.name: param_types
params.doc: One id per parameter, in call order. May be null when `param_count` is 0.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_create
functions.doc: Starts building a type descriptor.

params.name: canonical_name
params.doc: Stable name other code will look this type up by. Must not collide with an already-registered name.

params.name: size
params.doc: Size in bytes of one instance.

params.name: align
params.doc: Required alignment of one instance.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_discard
functions.doc: Discards `builder` without registering anything. Safe to call on an already-finished or already-discarded builder (a no-op).

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_finish
functions.doc: Finishes building and registers the type, consuming `builder`.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when the descriptor is incomplete (no `destroy` callback set) or `canonical_name` collides with a different, already-registered type.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_name
functions.doc: Reads a type's canonical name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_size
functions.doc: Reads a type's instance size/alignment — what `object` must point at `size` bytes of, aligned to `align`, for every instance-field/method call below.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_unregister_type
functions.doc: Unregisters a type, so no future `find_type`/field/method/event lookup can reach it — the mod-unload primitive. See `TypeRegistry::unregister_type`'s C++ doc comment for the full quiescence requirement: stop dispatching to this type (no calls in flight against it on any thread) *before* calling this, and only unload any shared library it came from after.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_unsubscribe_event
functions.doc: Removes a listener added by `sturdy_reflection_subscribe_event`.

functions.name: sturdy_relay_connect
functions.doc: Connects to a relay and waits for the partner. Object "tcp" connected to the partner: start TLS on it before sending anything private. `relay_tls` non-null: TLS to the relay itself. `timeout_ms` 0: 35 s.

functions.name: sturdy_relay_random_token
functions.doc: A fresh unguessable rendezvous token (32 hex characters).

functions.name: sturdy_relay_server_metrics
functions.doc: Counters as a finished op's fields: sessions_started, sessions_active, waiting, bytes_relayed, rejected, timed_out.

functions.name: sturdy_relay_server_start
functions.doc: Starts a rendezvous relay: pairs two connections that name the same token and forwards opaque bytes. It cannot read the peers' traffic when they run TLS through it. Object "relay_server". `authorize` may be null (any token is accepted).

functions.name: sturdy_render_create_mesh_model
functions.doc: Creates a renderable model from your own geometry.

params.name: vertices
params.doc: Vertex array. Must not be null.

params.name: vertex_count
params.doc: Number of vertices.

params.name: indices
params.doc: Triangle indices, three per triangle. Every index must be less than `vertex_count`; this is checked, because an out-of-range index would otherwise read past the vertex buffer on the GPU.

params.name: index_count
params.doc: Number of indices. Must be a multiple of three.

params.name: shader
params.doc: Shader the model draws with.

params.name: label
params.doc: Debug label, or null.

params.name: out_model
params.doc: Receives the model asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_create_shape_model
functions.doc: Creates a renderable model from a built-in shape.

params.name: shape
params.doc: Which shape to generate.

params.name: params
params.doc: Dimensions, previously initialized by `sturdy_render_shape_params_init`.

params.name: shader
params.doc: Shader the model draws with.

params.name: label
params.doc: Debug label, or null. Surfaced in graphics debuggers and engine logs.

params.name: out_model
params.doc: Receives the model asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_create_texture
functions.doc: Creates a texture asset directly from raw RGBA8 pixels — for a procedurally generated texture, as opposed to `sturdy_render_load_texture`/`sturdy_render_load_texture_from_memory`, which decode an encoded image format.

functions.name: sturdy_render_load_shader
functions.doc:
Loads a shader from a Slang source file.

A model needs a shader, and the engine's standard one is `"Shaders/gbuffer_geometry.slang"` with a depth-only entry point of `"depthOnlyMain"` — that pairing is what the deferred renderer expects, so pass it unless you have written your own.

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to the shader source, relative to the working directory unless absolute.

params.name: depth_only_entry_point
params.doc: Depth-only fragment entry point, or null for none.

params.name: out_shader
params.doc: Receives the shader asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_load_texture
functions.doc: Loads a texture from an encoded image file (PNG, JPEG, and the rest the engine decodes).

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to the image file.

params.name: srgb
params.doc: Nonzero to treat the contents as sRGB, which is right for color maps and wrong for normal and roughness maps.

params.name: out_texture
params.doc: Receives the texture asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_load_texture_from_memory
functions.doc: Decodes a texture from an in-memory encoded image (PNG, JPEG, and the rest the engine decodes) — the same decoder `sturdy_render_load_texture` uses, without requiring the bytes to already be a file on disk. For an image downloaded, generated, or packaged some other way.

params.name: encoded_bytes
params.doc: Encoded image bytes (a whole PNG/JPEG file's contents, not raw pixels).

params.name: encoded_size
params.doc: Length of `encoded_bytes`, in bytes. Must be nonzero.

params.name: srgb
params.doc: Nonzero to treat the contents as sRGB, which is right for color maps and wrong for normal and roughness maps.

params.name: out_texture
params.doc: Receives the texture asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_model_info
functions.doc: Reports how much geometry a model asset holds.

params.name: out_primitives
params.doc: Receives the primitive count. May be null.

params.name: out_vertices
params.doc: Receives the total vertex count. May be null.

params.name: out_triangles
params.doc: Receives the total triangle count. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_directional_light
functions.doc:
Makes an entity a directional light — the sun.

Direction comes from the entity's transform, so it needs one. Replaces any directional light the entity already has.

params.name: radiance
params.doc: Linear RGB radiance, three floats. Values well above 1 are normal for a sun.

params.name: angular_radius_degrees
params.doc: Apparent size, which is what softens shadow edges. The real sun is about 0.27.

params.name: casts_shadows
params.doc: Nonzero to render shadow maps for this light.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_light_direction
functions.doc:
Reads back an entity's world transform.

Writes the entity's `WorldTransform` rotation, leaving no translation. Lights are the only renderable whose transform is read as a direction rather than a placement, and the axis it is taken from is an engine-internal convention, so this exists rather than asking a caller to construct the matrix. Use `sturdy_render_set_transform` when a light also needs a position.

params.name: engine
params.doc: Engine handle supplied to a game-logic callback.

params.name: entity
params.doc: Entity carrying a light component.

params.name: x
params.doc: Direction x component, in world space, pointing the way light travels.

params.name: y
params.doc: Direction y component.

params.name: z
params.doc: Direction z component.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK`; `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when the direction is not finite or has zero length; a handle or entity error otherwise.
notes: This function does not throw exceptions.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model
functions.doc:
Makes an entity draw a model.

The entity also needs a transform to be drawn. Replaces any model the entity already has.

params.name: model
params.doc: Model asset to draw.

params.name: visible
params.doc: Nonzero to draw it. A hidden entity keeps its components and costs nothing to show again, which is cheaper than destroying and respawning it.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model_float
functions.doc: Sets a scalar material parameter on one of a model's primitives.

params.name: primitive
params.doc: Which primitive to affect; 0 for a single-shape model.

params.name: name
params.doc: Parameter name as the shader declares it.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model_texture
functions.doc: Binds a texture to a named slot on one of a model's primitives.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model_vec4
functions.doc: Sets a four-component material parameter on one of a model's primitives.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_point_light
functions.doc: Makes an entity a point light. Position comes from its transform.

params.name: radiance
params.doc: Linear RGB radiance, three floats.

params.name: range
params.doc: Distance beyond which the light contributes nothing.

params.name: source_radius
params.doc: Emitter radius, which softens shadows and highlights.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_spot_light
functions.doc: Makes an entity a spot light. Position and direction come from its transform.

params.name: radiance
params.doc: Linear RGB radiance, three floats.

params.name: range
params.doc: Distance beyond which the light contributes nothing.

params.name: inner_cone_degrees
params.doc: Half-angle of the fully lit cone.

params.name: outer_cone_degrees
params.doc: Half-angle at which the light has fallen off entirely. Must be at least `inner_cone_degrees`.

params.name: source_radius
params.doc: Emitter radius.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_transform
functions.doc:
Gives an entity a world transform.

Rendering is driven from the ECS: an entity with a transform and a model is drawn, an entity with a transform and a light lights the scene. These helpers write the engine's own components rather than making you reproduce their memory layout — which you could do through `sturdy_ecs_add_component`, but only by hard-coding a layout that is free to change.

Replaces any transform the entity already has.

params.name: matrix
params.doc: Column-major 4x4 model matrix, 16 floats. Must not be null.

functions.name: sturdy_render_shape_params_init
functions.doc: Fills `params` with the engine's default shape dimensions.

params.name: params
params.doc: Destination. Must not be null.

functions.name: sturdy_render_spawn
functions.doc:
Creates an entity ready to be rendered, carrying an identity transform.

The natural way to start a renderable: an entity must be spawned with at least one component, and the engine's own components register themselves lazily the first time something uses them — so looking `sturdy.engine.world_transform` up by name before anything has touched it reports `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE`. This registers it and spawns in one step.

Follow with `sturdy_render_set_transform` to place it and `sturdy_render_set_model` or one of the light setters to give it something to contribute.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the new entity.

functions.name: sturdy_render_texture_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with engine defaults (linear color space, mipmaps and compression both on) and the correct `struct_size`. `width`, `height`, and `rgba8` are left for the caller to set.

functions.name: sturdy_render_unload_asset
functions.doc:
Unloads an asset — a model, shader, or texture previously created by `sturdy_render_load_shader`, `sturdy_render_create_shape_model`, `sturdy_render_create_mesh_model`, or `sturdy_render_load_texture`. This is the only way to release one; without it, every asset a long-running caller creates accumulates for the life of the engine.

Unloading does not check whether an entity's `sturdy_render_set_model` still points at it — despawn or reassign every such entity first, or its next draw reads a destroyed asset.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` when `asset` is a shader or texture a loaded model still depends on; unload that model first. `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` when `asset` does not name a live asset.

functions.name: sturdy_restir_gi_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (Medium quality, SVGF denoiser, disabled — ReSTIR GI is opt-in).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes
functions.doc: Queries the buffer sizes needed to build the acceleration structure described by `desc`. `desc->dst`/`src` are ignored; only `type`, `flags`, and `geometries` matter for sizing.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_device_address
functions.doc: Reads the GPU virtual address of `structure`, for writing into `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance::acceleration_structure_device_address`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_adapter_info
functions.doc: Reads the active adapter's numeric identity.

params.name: out_info
params.doc: Destination. Must not be null; `struct_size` is written by the engine.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_adapter_string
functions.doc: Reads one of the adapter's text fields. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_backend
functions.doc:
Reports which graphics backend the engine actually created.

This is the resolved answer, never `STURDY_BACKEND_DEFAULT`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_buffer_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (`STURDY_MEMORY_LOCATION_DEVICE_LOCAL`, no usage flags, zero size).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_buffer_device_address
functions.doc: Reads the GPU virtual address of `buffer`. Requires the buffer to have been created with storage/indirect/acceleration-structure-input usage that publishes a device address on the active backend.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_barrier
functions.doc: Inserts a pipeline barrier. Any of the three arrays may be empty (count 0, pointer null).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_begin_compute_pass
functions.doc: Begins a compute pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_begin_pipeline_statistics_query
functions.doc: Begins a pipeline-statistics query at `query_set[index]`, ended by `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_end_pipeline_statistics_query`. Only valid for a `STURDY_QUERY_TYPE_PIPELINE_STATISTICS` query set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_begin_render_pass
functions.doc: Begins a render pass. `desc->color_attachments` is read synchronously and need not outlive the call.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_build_acceleration_structures
functions.doc: Builds or updates `build_count` acceleration structures, recorded into the command encoder outside any render/compute pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_build_opacity_micromaps
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_clear_color_texture
functions.doc: Clears a color texture's subresources to a solid color, outside any render pass.
notes: `texture` must have been created with `STURDY_TEXTURE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT`. Vulkan's `vkCmdClearColorImage` has no such requirement, but D3D12 clears through a render-target view, so this is required for portability across both backends even though only one enforces it — verified empirically against both.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_clear_depth_stencil_texture
functions.doc: Clears a depth/stencil texture's subresources, outside any render pass.
notes: `texture` should be created with `STURDY_TEXTURE_USAGE_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT`; by symmetry with `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_clear_color_texture` above, D3D12 likely clears through a depth-stencil view the same way, though this has not been independently verified against both backends the way the color case was.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_buffer_to_buffer
functions.doc: Copies bytes between two buffers.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_buffer_to_texture
functions.doc: Copies bytes from a buffer into a texture's subresources.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_texture_to_buffer
functions.doc: Copies texels from a texture's subresources into a buffer.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_texture_to_texture
functions.doc: Copies texels between two textures' subresources.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (graphics queue, lane 0).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_end_pipeline_statistics_query
functions.doc: Ends the most recently begun pipeline-statistics query on this encoder.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_fill_buffer
functions.doc: Fills a byte range of `buffer` with repeated copies of `value`, outside any render/compute pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_finish
functions.doc: Ends recording and produces a submittable command buffer. `encoder` is consumed: its token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_pop_debug_group
functions.doc: Pops the most recently pushed debug group.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_push_debug_group
functions.doc: Pushes a labeled debug group, for graphics-debugger capture readability.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_release
functions.doc: Abandons an in-progress recording without submitting it. Use `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_finish` instead when the recorded commands should actually run.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_reset_query_set
functions.doc: Resets `count` queries starting at `first` to the unavailable state, recorded into the command encoder.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_resolve_query_set
functions.doc: Copies `count` query results starting at `first` from `query_set` into `dst` at `dst_offset`, entirely on the GPU. Prefer this over `sturdy_rhi_get_query_set_results` when the results feed a later GPU pass rather than the host (e.g. GPU-driven culling statistics).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_set_ray_tracing_pipeline
functions.doc: Binds the ray tracing pipeline used by a subsequent `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_trace_rays`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_trace_rays
functions.doc: Dispatches rays against the pipeline bound by `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_set_ray_tracing_pipeline`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_update_buffer
functions.doc: Records a GPU-timed write of `data` into `buffer` at `offset`, outside any render/compute pass. Prefer this over `sturdy_rhi_write_buffer` for a write that must be ordered against other commands in the same encoder.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_write_timestamp
functions.doc: Writes a GPU timestamp for `query_set[index]` once every command before this point in the encoder has reached `stage`. Only valid for a `STURDY_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP` query set.

params.name: stage
params.doc: A single `STURDY_PIPELINE_STAGE_*` value (not a combination) naming the point in the pipeline to timestamp.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_compute_pass_dispatch_indirect
functions.doc: Dispatches using group counts read from `indirect_buffer` at `offset` (three consecutive `uint32_t`s), written by an earlier pass on the GPU.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_compute_pass_end
functions.doc: Ends the compute pass. `pass`'s token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails. The parent command encoder may be used again afterward.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group
functions.doc: Creates a bind group. `desc->entries` is read synchronously and need not outlive the call. The group is created persistent (not frame-transient); destroy it explicitly when done.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group_layout
functions.doc: Creates a bind group layout. `desc->entries` is read synchronously and need not outlive the call.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_buffer
functions.doc: Creates a buffer on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_command_encoder
functions.doc: Begins recording a new command buffer.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_compute_pipeline
functions.doc: Creates a compute pipeline on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_fence
functions.doc: Creates a fence on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_opacity_micromap
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_pipeline_layout
functions.doc: Creates a pipeline layout. `desc->bind_group_layouts`/`push_constant_ranges` are read synchronously and need not outlive the call.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_query_set
functions.doc: Creates a query set on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_render_bundle_encoder
functions.doc: Begins recording a render bundle.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_render_pipeline
functions.doc: Creates a render pipeline on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_sampler
functions.doc: Creates a sampler on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_semaphore
functions.doc: Creates a semaphore on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_shader_module
functions.doc: Creates a shader module. `desc->language` must match what the active backend consumes (`STURDY_SHADER_LANGUAGE_SPIRV` for Vulkan, `STURDY_SHADER_LANGUAGE_DXIL` for D3D12); check `sturdy_rhi_backend` first if targeting both.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_texture
functions.doc: Creates a texture on the engine's active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_texture_view
functions.doc: Creates a texture view. `desc->texture` must be a live handle from `sturdy_rhi_create_texture`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_acceleration_structure
functions.doc: Destroys an acceleration structure. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_bind_group
functions.doc: Destroys a bind group created by `sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_bind_group_layout
functions.doc: Destroys a bind group layout created by `sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group_layout`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_buffer
functions.doc: Destroys a buffer created by `sturdy_rhi_create_buffer`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_command_buffer
functions.doc: Destroys a command buffer produced by `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_finish`, whether or not it was submitted. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_compute_pipeline
functions.doc: Destroys a compute pipeline created by `sturdy_rhi_create_compute_pipeline`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_fence
functions.doc: Destroys a fence created by `sturdy_rhi_create_fence`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_opacity_micromap
functions.doc: Destroys an opacity micromap. A null/zero handle is a no-op; always safe to call even on D3D12, where it is a no-op regardless of the handle.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_pipeline_layout
functions.doc: Destroys a pipeline layout created by `sturdy_rhi_create_pipeline_layout`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_query_set
functions.doc: Destroys a query set created by `sturdy_rhi_create_query_set`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_render_bundle
functions.doc: Destroys a bundle created by `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_finish`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_render_pipeline
functions.doc: Destroys a render pipeline created by `sturdy_rhi_create_render_pipeline`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_sampler
functions.doc: Destroys a sampler created by `sturdy_rhi_create_sampler`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_semaphore
functions.doc: Destroys a semaphore created by `sturdy_rhi_create_semaphore`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_shader_module
functions.doc: Destroys a shader module created by `sturdy_rhi_create_shader_module`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_texture
functions.doc: Destroys a texture created by `sturdy_rhi_create_texture`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_texture_view
functions.doc: Destroys a texture view created by `sturdy_rhi_create_texture_view`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_device_limits
functions.doc: Reads the active device's hardware limits.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_extension_count
functions.doc: Returns how many RHI extensions are enabled on the active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_extension_name
functions.doc: Reads the enabled extension at `index` as `"<namespace>.<name>"`, with its version.

params.name: out_version
params.doc: Receives the extension version. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_count
functions.doc:
Returns how many RHI features exist in this engine build.

Features are addressed by index rather than by a mirrored C enum on purpose: the engine defines several hundred of them and adds more over time, and restating that list here would guarantee the two drift apart. Enumerate names with `sturdy_rhi_feature_name`, or resolve a known name to its index once at startup with `sturdy_rhi_feature_index`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_enabled
functions.doc: Reports whether the feature at `index` was actually enabled on the active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_index
functions.doc: Resolves a feature name to its index.

params.name: name
params.doc: Null-terminated feature name, matching `sturdy_rhi_feature_name` exactly.

params.name: out_index
params.doc: Receives the index.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when this build has no feature by that name — which is also how a binding detects that it is running against an older engine.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of the feature at `index`. See the string-output convention above.

params.name: index
params.doc: Feature index, less than `sturdy_rhi_feature_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_get_query_set_results
functions.doc: Reads back `count` results starting at `first`, into `dst` (which must be at least `count * stride` bytes). Blocks the host if `STURDY_QUERY_RESULT_FLAGS_WAIT` is set; otherwise a query whose result is not yet available reads as undefined unless `STURDY_QUERY_RESULT_FLAGS_PARTIAL` is also set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_map_buffer
functions.doc: Maps `buffer` for host access. Only valid for a buffer created with a host-visible `SturdyMemoryLocation`.

params.name: out_ptr
params.doc: Receives a pointer to the mapped range, valid until `sturdy_rhi_unmap_buffer`.

params.name: out_size
params.doc: Receives the mapped range's size in bytes. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_opacity_micromap_build_sizes
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_pack_instance_custom_index_and_mask
functions.doc: Packs a 24-bit custom index and 8-bit visibility mask into `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance::custom_index_and_mask`. Pure host-side bit packing — takes no engine handle and cannot fail.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_pack_instance_sbt_offset_and_flags
functions.doc: Packs a 24-bit shader binding table offset and 8-bit instance flags into `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance::shader_binding_table_offset_and_flags`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_queue_count
functions.doc: Returns how many queue families the active device exposes.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_queue_info
functions.doc: Reads the queue family at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_ray_tracing_pipeline_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (`max_ray_recursion_depth = 1`, no groups).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and zeroed contents (no color formats, no depth/stencil format, `samples = 1`) — set `color_formats` before use.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect
functions.doc: D3D12 does not allow indirect draws of any kind — including mesh-tasks-indirect — inside a bundle; this reports a backend failure there rather than an ABI-level rejection, matching how the ordinary indirect-draw bundle restriction behaves.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect_count
functions.doc: See `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect`'s D3D12 caveat.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_finish
functions.doc: Finishes recording, consuming `encoder` (its token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails) and producing a replayable `SturdyRenderBundle`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_release
functions.doc: Abandons an in-progress bundle recording without finishing it. `encoder`'s token is invalid after this call.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_set_bind_group
functions.doc: Binds a bind group at `index`. Same `dynamic_offsets` convention as `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_bind_group`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_begin_occlusion_query
functions.doc: Begins an occlusion query at `query_set[index]`, ended by `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end_occlusion_query`. Only valid for a `STURDY_QUERY_TYPE_OCCLUSION` query set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and zeroed contents (no color attachments, no depth/stencil attachment, zero render area — set `color_attachments`/`render_area` before use).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indexed_indirect
functions.doc: Indexed counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indexed_indirect_count
functions.doc: Indexed counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indexed_indirect_multi
functions.doc: Indexed counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_multi`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect
functions.doc: Draws using arguments read from `indirect_buffer` at `offset` (a single `SturdyDrawArgs`-shaped record, engine-native layout matching the active backend's indirect-draw structure).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count
functions.doc: Issues up to `max_draws` draws read from `indirect_buffer`, with the actual count read from a 32-bit value in `count_buffer` at `count_offset` (clamped to `max_draws`). Backed by `vkCmdDrawIndirectCount` on Vulkan and `ExecuteIndirect` with a counter resource on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_multi
functions.doc: Issues `draw_count` draws read from consecutive `stride`-byte records in `indirect_buffer` starting at `offset`. `draw_count` is fixed at record time; use `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count` when the count itself comes from the GPU.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_mesh_tasks
functions.doc: Dispatches the mesh (and, if present, task) shader stages of the currently bound pipeline, which must have been created with `SturdyRenderPipelineDesc::mesh` set. Neither backend clamps `group_count_*` against a device maximum here — an out-of-range value is a backend- defined failure, the same as a C++ caller would see.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect
functions.doc: Mesh-shader counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect`: dispatch dimensions are read from a single `SturdyDrawMeshTasksArgs`-shaped record in `indirect_buffer` at `offset`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect_count
functions.doc: Mesh-shader counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end
functions.doc: Ends the render pass. `pass`'s token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails. The parent command encoder may be used again afterward.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end_occlusion_query
functions.doc: Ends the most recently begun occlusion query on this render pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_execute_bundles
functions.doc: Replays `bundles` into `pass`, which must have been created with `SturdyRenderPassDesc::allow_bundles` set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_bind_group
functions.doc: Binds a bind group at `index`. `dynamic_offsets` supplies one offset per dynamic-offset binding in the group's layout, in declaration order; pass null/0 when the layout has none.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_blend_constant
functions.doc: Sets the constant blend color used by `STURDY_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR`/ `STURDY_BLEND_FACTOR_ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_index_buffer
functions.doc: Binds the index buffer used by subsequent indexed draws.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_pipeline
functions.doc: Sets the pipeline used by subsequent draws.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_push_constants
functions.doc: Writes push-constant bytes visible to `stages`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_vertex_buffer
functions.doc: Binds a vertex buffer at `slot`, matching the pipeline's `vertex_buffers` layout array index.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pipeline_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (triangle list, fill/back-cull/CCW rasterization, no multisampling, no depth/stencil, no color targets, zeroed shader entries).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_reset_fences
functions.doc: Resets one or more fences to unsignaled.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_reset_query_set
functions.doc: Resets `count` queries starting at `first` to the unavailable state, outside any command encoder. Every query must be reset (via this or `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_reset_query_set`) before its first use.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_sampler_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (linear filtering/mipmapping, repeat addressing, LOD range [0, 1000], no anisotropy, no comparison).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_semaphore_value
functions.doc: Reads the semaphore's current counter value.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_signal_semaphore
functions.doc: Advances `semaphore`'s counter to `value` from the host. Rarely needed directly — a submission with a signal entry (see `sturdy_rhi_submit`) is the usual way a semaphore advances.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_submit
functions.doc: Submits finished command buffers to a device queue for execution.

params.name: fence
params.doc: Optional; the zero handle submits with no fence. When supplied, it becomes signaled once this submission's work completes — wait on it with `sturdy_rhi_wait_fences` rather than `sturdy_rhi_wait_idle` to know when it is safe to reuse or destroy the submitted command buffers. This is the one-shot GPU-work pattern: create a fence, submit with it, wait on it, destroy the fence and command buffer.

params.name: one_shot
params.doc: Hints that these command buffers will not be resubmitted, letting the backend release their recording resources as soon as this submission completes.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_texture_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (2D, `STURDY_FORMAT_UNDEFINED`, 1x1x1, one mip level, one sample, no usage flags).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_unmap_buffer
functions.doc: Unmaps a buffer previously mapped with `sturdy_rhi_map_buffer`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_wait_fences
